480 class CUDAWarmupNode:
481     """
482     Simplified Wrapper around A CUDA Model that wraps outputs in storage refs and exposes
483     apis to get the live storages in the current chain of warmup.
484 
485     A CUDAWarmupNode may have either CUDAGraphNode or CUDAWarmupNode as a parent, but may only have
486     CUDAWarmupNode as children, because we cannot record or execute with tensors which do not have stable
487     memory addresses.
488 
489     CUDAWarmupNode and CUDAGraphNode have a number of differences that make it easier to use separate classes.
490     - Much of the CUDAGraphNode logic & initialization is based on the tensor properties of first recording. In the
491     first instance of warmup, these are not finalized yet.
492     - All Inputs to the RecordedFunction must be copied over to the cuda graph memory pool, this is unnecessary in warmup.
493     - CUDAWarmup is only used once and so does not need to optimize as much bookkeeping. It is much simpler.
494 
495     NB: this class and CUDAGraphNode need to expose `path_live_weakrefs`, `all_outputs_are_dead`, and
496     `self.outputs_weakrefs` for compatibility.
497     """
498 
499     def __init__(
500         self,
501         wrapped_function: WrappedFunction,
502         parent,
503         cuda_graphs_pool: Tuple[int, int],
504         existing_cuda_graph: torch.cuda.Graph,
505         device_index: int,
506         stack_traces: Optional[StackTraces],
507         stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
508         already_warm: bool,
509     ):
510         self.wrapped_function = wrapped_function
511         self.parent = parent
512         self.cuda_graphs_pool = cuda_graphs_pool
513         self.outputs_weakrefs: List[Optional[StorageWeakRefWrapper]] = []
514         self.existing_cuda_graph = existing_cuda_graph
515         self.has_run = False
516         self.device_index = device_index
517         self.stack_traces = stack_traces
518         self.stream = stream
519         self.already_warm = already_warm
520 
521     def run(self, new_inputs):
522         assert not self.has_run, "Wrapped function should never be run twice"
523 
524         # See: output_is_alias_of_persistent_static_inputs below. We should only be returning freshly created
525         # storages in path_live_weakrefs.
526         existing_path_data_ptrs = {
527             t.data_ptr() for t in self.path_live_weakrefs() if t()
528         }
529         non_cudagraph_inps = set()
530         for i in range(len(new_inputs)):
531             if (
532                 new_inputs[i].untyped_storage().data_ptr()
533                 not in existing_path_data_ptrs
534             ):
535                 non_cudagraph_inps.add(new_inputs[i].untyped_storage().data_ptr())
536 
537         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts and not self.already_warm:
538             refs = list(self.path_live_weakrefs())
539             check_memory_pool(self.device_index, self.cuda_graphs_pool, refs)
540 
541         with torch.cuda.device(
542             self.device_index
543         ), clear_cublas_manager(), _use_cuda_memory_pool_manager(
544             self.device_index, self.cuda_graphs_pool, self.stream
545         ), get_history_recording():
546             out = self.wrapped_function.model(new_inputs)
547 
548         # sync up stream used in `_use_cuda_memory_pool_manager` - TODO - wait stream instead ?
549         torch.cuda.synchronize()
550 
551         assert len(new_inputs) == 0
552 
553         self.outputs_weakrefs.extend(
554             [
555                 map_to_ref(o)
556                 for o in out
557                 if o is not None
558                 and o.untyped_storage().data_ptr() not in non_cudagraph_inps
559             ]
560         )
561 
562         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts and not self.already_warm:
563             out_refs = self.path_live_weakrefs()
564             new_storages = [
565                 t for t in out_refs if t.data_ptr() not in non_cudagraph_inps
566             ]
567             check_memory_pool(self.device_index, self.cuda_graphs_pool, new_storages)
568 
569         return out
570 
571     def path_live_weakrefs(self) -> Generator[StorageWeakRefWrapper]:
572         "Returns all live storages weakrefs that created by nodes in this path"
573         for stor_ref, _ in self.path_live_weakrefs_and_stacktraces():
574             yield stor_ref
575 
576     def path_live_weakrefs_and_stacktraces(
577         self,
578     ) -> Generator[Tuple[StorageWeakRefWrapper, Optional[str]]]:
579         nodes = []
580         node = self
581         while node:
582             nodes.append(node)
583             node = node.parent
584 
585         for node in reversed(nodes):
586             for i, output in enumerate(node.outputs_weakrefs):
587                 if is_live(output):
588                     yield output, (node.stack_traces[i] if node.stack_traces else None)
589 
590     def all_outputs_are_dead(self):
591         return not list(self.path_live_weakrefs())

632 class CUDAGraphNode:
633     """
634     A single recording of a function into a CUDA Graph. Recordings of CUDA Graphs share a single memory pool
635     and are structured into a tree, where there is a single recording that can precede it (parent) and multiple
636     subsequent recordings that may follow (children). A node will have no parent if it is the first recording
637     in a tree; i.e., when it is first recorded, there are no live tensors from a previous recording which
638     would force a dependency.
639 
640     On first recording, all of the live tensors in the current CUDA Graph Node path will be
641     reflected in the corresponding private pool. On subsequent executions, the caching allocator
642     is unaffected when the graph is replayed.
643 
644     In order to support recording a subsequent cuda graph recording after execution of this graph,
645     we checkpoint the state of the memory pool so that it may later be resumed.
646 
647     WrappedFunction should have already been warmed up prior to invocation.
648 
649     See [setCheckpointPoolState] for further explanation, as well as
650     https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13564/222815509-374f3400-f83d-4f7d-8fa6-4a092b3250bb.png
651     """
652 
653     def __init__(
654         self,
655         wrapped_function: WrappedFunction,
656         id: GraphID,
657         parent: Optional[CUDAGraphNode],
658         inputs: List[Tensor],
659         cuda_graphs_pool: Tuple[int, int],
660         device_index: int,
661         stack_traces: Optional[StackTraces],
662         stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
663     ):
664         assert isinstance(inputs, (list, tuple))
665 
666         self.wrapped_function = wrapped_function
667         self.id = id
668         self.device = device_index
669         self.stack_traces = stack_traces
670         self.stream = stream
671 
672         # if this is a root parent will be None. use weakref to prevent reference cycle
673         self._parent = weakref.ref(parent) if parent is not None else None
674         # reference to the shared memory pool for the entire cuda graphs tree
675         self.cuda_graphs_pool = cuda_graphs_pool
676 
677         # A single wrapped function may be recorded multiple times if memory patterns or
678         # invariants change from one execution to the next
679         self.children: Dict[FunctionID, List[CUDAGraphNode]] = defaultdict(list)
680 
681         # StorageWeakRef maintains whether the Storage C++ object remains allocated,
682         # not whether the corresponding memory has been deallocated. In order
683         # to use them to track memory deallocations we must maintain a single StorageWeakRef
684         # for all Storages that reference that memory (even if we are constructing Storages
685         # that do not have a deallocator function). We maintain one single storage_cache
686         # as we execute any tree path. When we retrieve a storage from the cache we
687         # check that it is still alive, and we hash based on observed recording data ptr
688         # and storage cdata.
689 
690         # we preserve a single reference to executed outputs that is then referenced
691         # in children to avoid children having to chase parent pointers in the hot path
692         # DO NOT reassign output_weakrefs, only call `clear()`
693         # Path is a series of nodes from root to the current node
694         self.outputs_weakrefs: OutputList[Optional[StorageWeakRefWrapper]] = []
695         self.path_weakrefs: LevelList[OutputList[Optional[StorageWeakRefWrapper]]] = [
696             node.outputs_weakrefs for node in self._path_from_root
697         ]
698         self.path_stacktraces: LevelList[StackTraces] = [
699             node.stack_traces for node in self._path_from_root
700         ]
701 
702         # tensors which are outputs of previous graphs in the tree
703         self.cudagraph_managed_idxs: List[int] = [
704             idx
705             for idx, t in enumerate(inputs)
706             if self._is_cuda_graph_recorded_tensor(t)
707         ]
708 
709         self.static_input_idxs: List[int] = list(
710             set(wrapped_function.static_input_idxs) | set(self.cudagraph_managed_idxs)
711         )
712 
713         self.static_input_data_ptrs: InputList[int] = [
714             (inputs[i].data_ptr() if i in self.static_input_idxs else None)
715             for i in range(len(inputs))
716         ]
717 
718         # When we checkpoint, and free generations, we will be manually freeing the outputs
719         # of CUDAGraphNodes. We should not be freeing parameters, not do we need to account for
720         # their liveness (they are static), so we need to compute which outputs are aliases of
721         # parameters. Some static inputs are saved tensors from the forward that die in the backward.
722         # Their locations are static but lifetimes are not. We only include the persistent static
723         # data ptrs below because the non persistent data ptrs may be outputs of this record and
724         # fresh allocations.
725 
726         # precompute expanded dims to avoid computing in the hot path
727         self.expanded_dims: List[List[int]] = [
728             get_expanded_dims(x) if idx not in self.static_input_idxs else []
729             for idx, x in enumerate(inputs)
730         ]
731 
732         # For each node in path, which outputs were observed to be live
733         # before invoking graph recording, and after graph recording
734         self.recorded_liveness_before_graph: LevelList[OutputList[bool]] = []
735         self.recorded_liveness_after_graph: LevelList[OutputList[bool]] = []
736 
737         # List of Tuples of (depth, output_index) that index into node at depth
738         # number of nodes from root and output_index of outputs. Will index into
739         # path_weakrefs.
740         self.expected_dead_indices_before_graph: List[PathOutputIndex] = []
741         self.expected_dead_indices_after_graph: List[PathOutputIndex] = []
742 
743         # all live indices after graph recording
744         self.live_indices_after_graph: List[PathOutputIndex] = []
745 
746         if self.parent is not None:
747             previous_liveness = self.parent.recorded_liveness_after_graph
748             curr_liveness = self._get_liveness(self.path_weakrefs)
749 
750             different_indices = self._get_different_indices(
751                 previous_liveness, curr_liveness
752             )
753 
754             self.recorded_liveness_before_graph = curr_liveness
755             self.expected_dead_indices_before_graph = different_indices
756 
757         recording_inputs = self._allocate_and_copy_recording_inputs(inputs)
758         # recording inputs will copy over memory, so we can free non recording inputs
759         inputs.clear()
760         del inputs
761 
762         # graph used for recording model invocation
763         self.graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
764 
765         # we allocate non-static inputs within the same memory pool as the CUDAGraph
766         # which we will record the model with. For memory efficiency, it is important
767         # to reclaim the input memory when the inputs are no longer live. To accomplish this,
768         # we reconstruct tensors at the correct data pointers of our inputs which are
769         # non owning and do not prevent deallocation. On subsequent executions, input values
770         # will be copied over to these tensors.
771         self.reconstructed_inputs: InputList[Tensor] = [
772             self._reconstruct_from_tensor_metadata(self._tensor_metadata(x))
773             for x in recording_inputs
774         ]
775 
776         # DO THE RECORDING!!!
777         # We record the CUDA graph in the constructor of CUDAGraphNode, which
778         # gives you what the CPU side compute of the function would do.  We
779         # don't throw the recording outputs away: their memory is
780         # correctly accounted for in the CUDAGraphs caching allocator.  This
781         # means on the very FIRST run of the CUDA graph node, we can directly
782         # do more recording, because we have a valid caching allocator state.
783         # NB: This relies on run() being called immediately after the
784         # constructor, otherwise this optimization would not be valid.
785 
786         # initialized below in _record
787 
788         self.checkpointed_caching_state: Optional[AllocatorState] = None
789 
790         # Output Storage Alias information, can be:
791         # - A new, unaliased storage, or the output is None
792         # - An alias of an output of a prior graph
793         # - An alias of an output already created in the reconstructed outputs
794         self.output_storage_alias: OutputList[OutputAliasInfo] = []
795 
796         # is the output Storage unaliased in subsequent outputs, of all subsequent paths
797         # if it is, we cached the output tensor and adjust storage liveness tracking to also
798         # check if the output tensor does not have an additional python reference.
799         # If a descendent node discovers it has an alias of a prior output, then the output
800         # will no longer be cached in the ancestor.
801         # The large majority of tensors are unaliased, and preserving aliased output tensors would add
802         # significant additional complexity with marginal gains
803         # The cached tensor outputs are added on the first execution, and cleared whenever we need
804         # to do subsequent recording
805         self.unaliased_in_all_paths: OutputList[bool] = []
806         self.cached_tensor_outputs: OutputList[Optional[Tensor]] = []
807 
808         # if an output aliases a static, persistent input then the corresponding Tensor will
809         # be set here. These are different than cached tensors, because they are tensors that
810         # are aliases of parameters that are always live.
811         self.static_output_tensors: OutputList[Optional[Tensor]] = []
812 
813         self.recording_outputs: OutputList[Optional[torch.Tensor]] = self._record(
814             wrapped_function.model, recording_inputs
815         )
816         self.outputs_metadata: OutputList[Optional[Dict[str, Any]]] = []
817 
818         # As with inputs, we do not want to keep the outputs permanently alive because that would prevent
819         # their memory being reclaimed in subsequent cuda graph recordings. We record the tensor metadata
820         # needed to reconstruct instead.
821         for out in self.recording_outputs:
822             if isinstance(out, torch.Tensor):
823                 self.outputs_metadata.append(
824                     self._tensor_metadata(out, ignore_storage_offset=False)
825                 )
826             else:
827                 assert out is None
828                 self.outputs_metadata.append(None)
829 
830         self.graph.replay()
831 
832     def _copy_input(self, idx, dst, src):
833         expanded_dims = self.expanded_dims[idx]
834         dst = index_expanded_dims(dst, expanded_dims)
835         src = index_expanded_dims(src, expanded_dims)
836         # TODO - one jit kernel across multiple inputs
837         dst.copy_(src)
838 
839     def run_first_inputs(self, new_inputs):
840         if config.triton.fast_path_cudagraph_asserts:
841             self.debug_check_invariants_before_invocation()
842 
843         # graph is already invoked in the __init__
844         # inputs are copied over in _allocate_recording_inputs and subsequently cleared
845         assert len(new_inputs) == 0
846         outputs = self.recording_outputs
847         self.recording_outputs = None
848         return outputs
849 
850     def run(self, new_inputs):
851         if config.triton.fast_path_cudagraph_asserts:
852             self.debug_check_invariants_before_invocation()
853 
854         assert len(self.static_input_data_ptrs) == len(new_inputs)
855         # NB: this ranges over non-static inputs too
856         for idx, data_ptr in enumerate(self.static_input_data_ptrs):
857             if idx in self.cudagraph_managed_idxs:
858                 continue
859             if data_ptr is not None:
860                 # static input, e.g., parameter
861                 assert data_ptr == new_inputs[idx].data_ptr()
862             else:
863                 # non-static input, need to copy it into CUDA graph
864                 dst = self.reconstructed_inputs[idx]
865                 src = new_inputs[idx]
866                 self._copy_input(idx, dst, src)
867 
868         new_inputs.clear()
869         self.run_graph()
870 
871         outputs = self.reconstruct_outputs()
872         self.debug_check_invariants_after_invocation()
873 
874         return outputs
875 
876     def reconstruct_outputs(self):
877         "Reconstruct output tensors according to their saved metadata and alias information"
878 
879         # Cached tensors will not yet be set on the first execution
880         # They are also cleared in checkpointing, so if we checkpoint this node
881         # and then execute it again we will need to repopulate cached tensors
882         if not self.cached_tensor_outputs:
883             self._initialize_cached_tensors()
884 
885         outputs = []
886 
887         for i, (storage_info, metadata) in enumerate(
888             zip(self.output_storage_alias, self.outputs_metadata)
889         ):
890             if metadata is None:
891                 outputs.append(None)
892                 continue
893 
894             cached_t = self.cached_tensor_outputs[i]
895             if cached_t is not None:
896                 # No need to update weakrefs, already correctly initialized
897                 outputs.append(cached_t)
898                 continue
899 
900             static_t = self.static_output_tensors[i]
901             if static_t is not None:
902                 assert self.outputs_weakrefs[i] is None

907                 storage_info, metadata

911                 out = self._reconstruct_from_tensor_metadata(metadata, storage)

913                 assert isinstance(storage, int)

915                     metadata, outputs[storage].untyped_storage()

962     def _record(self, model, inputs):
963         "Record the model"
964 
965         # see: output_is_alias_of_persistent_static_inputs above
966         static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs: Dict[int, StorageWeakRefWrapper] = {
967             inputs[i].untyped_storage().data_ptr(): StorageWeakRefWrapper(inputs[i])
968             for i in self.wrapped_function.static_input_idxs
969             if not self._is_cuda_graph_recorded_tensor(inputs[i])
970         }
971 
972         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts:
973             # need to use parent live weakrefs because live_indices isnt set yet
974             memory = (
975                 [] if self.parent is None else list(self.parent.path_live_weakrefs())
976             )
977             memory += [
978                 StorageWeakRefWrapper(elem)
979                 for i, elem in enumerate(inputs)
980                 if i not in self.wrapped_function.static_input_idxs
981             ]
982             check_memory_pool(self.device, self.cuda_graphs_pool, memory)
983 
984         with preserve_rng_state(), torch.cuda.device(
985             self.device
986         ), clear_cublas_manager(), torch.cuda.graph(
987             self.graph, stream=self.stream, pool=self.cuda_graphs_pool
988         ), get_history_recording():
989             static_outputs = model(inputs)
990 
991         # running model should reclaim memory
992         assert len(inputs) == 0
993 
994         if not isinstance(static_outputs, (list, tuple)):
995             static_outputs = (static_outputs,)
996 
997         self._add_first_outputs(static_outputs, static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs)
998 
999         return static_outputs

1001     def _add_first_outputs(
1002         self,
1003         outputs,
1004         static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs: Dict[int, StorageWeakRefWrapper],
1005     ):
1006         "Add the outputs from the first invocation of the node and set up metadata"
1007 
1008         # getting liveness before we have added the outputs to path, so the length
1009         # of the two lists is equal
1010         prev_liveness = self.recorded_liveness_before_graph
1011         curr_liveness = self._get_liveness(self.path_weakrefs)
1012 
1013         delta = self._get_different_indices(prev_liveness, curr_liveness)
1014         self.expected_dead_indices_after_graph = delta
1015 
1016         assert len(self.outputs_weakrefs) == 0
1017         # index from data pointer to index in outputs
1018         output_new_storages_index: Dict[StorageDataPtr, int] = {}
1019 
1020         self.unaliased_in_all_paths = [False for _ in range(len(outputs))]
1021         self.static_output_tensors = [None for _ in range(len(outputs))]
1022 
1023         for i, o in enumerate(outputs):
1024             if o is None:
1025                 self.output_storage_alias.append(UnaliasedStorage)
1026                 continue
1027 
1028             ref = static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs.get(
1029                 o.untyped_storage().data_ptr(), None
1030             )
1031             if ref and ref() is not None:
1032                 self.output_storage_alias.append(None)
1033                 self.static_output_tensors[i] = o
1034                 continue
1035 
1036             path_ref = self._is_alias_of_live_recorded_tensor(o)
1037             if path_ref is not None:
1038                 self._mark_prior_graph_output_as_aliased(path_ref)
1039                 self.output_storage_alias.append(AliasesPriorGraphOutput(path_ref))
1040                 continue
1041 
1042             if o.untyped_storage().data_ptr() in output_new_storages_index:
1043                 index = output_new_storages_index[o.untyped_storage().data_ptr()]
1044                 self.unaliased_in_all_paths[index] = False
1045                 self.output_storage_alias.append(AliasesNewOutput(index))
1046                 continue
1047 
1048             output_new_storages_index[o.untyped_storage().data_ptr()] = i
1049             self.output_storage_alias.append(UnaliasedStorage)
1050             self.unaliased_in_all_paths[i] = True
1051 
1052         if self.stack_traces is None:
1053             self.stack_traces = [None for _ in range(len(outputs))]
1054         else:
1055             assert len(self.stack_traces) == len(
1056                 outputs
1057             ), "Wrong number of stack traces passed in"
1058 
1059         assert not self.outputs_weakrefs
1060         for out, static_output_tensor in zip(outputs, self.static_output_tensors):
1061             if out is None or static_output_tensor is not None:
1062                 self.outputs_weakrefs.append(None)
1063             else:
1064                 self.outputs_weakrefs.append(StorageWeakRefWrapper(out))
1065 
1066         self.recorded_liveness_after_graph = self._get_liveness(self.path_weakrefs)
1067         self.checkpointed_caching_state = torch._C._cuda_getCheckpointState(
1068             self.device, self.cuda_graphs_pool
1069         )
1070 
1071         # now, get liveness with outputs added
1072         for depth in range(len(self.path_weakrefs)):
1073             for output_index in range(len(self.path_weakrefs[depth])):
1074                 if is_live(self.path_weakrefs[depth][output_index]):
1075                     self.live_indices_after_graph.append((depth, output_index))
1076 
1077         self.debug_check_invariants_after_invocation()
1078         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts:
1079             check_memory_pool(
1080                 self.device, self.cuda_graphs_pool, list(self.path_live_weakrefs())
1081             )

1090     def _initialize_cached_tensors(self):
1091         # we should not be clearing output_weakrefs, and they should be set in the first
1092         # record run
1093         assert len(self.outputs_weakrefs) == len(self.outputs_metadata)
1094 
1095         for i, (storage_info, metadata, make_cached) in enumerate(
1096             zip(
1097                 self.output_storage_alias,
1098                 self.outputs_metadata,
1099                 self.unaliased_in_all_paths,
1100             )
1101         ):
1102             if not make_cached:
1103                 self.cached_tensor_outputs.append(None)
1104                 continue
1105 
1106             assert storage_info is UnaliasedStorage
1107             s = self.create_storage(metadata)
1108             out = self._reconstruct_from_tensor_metadata(metadata, storage=s)
1109 
1110             # XXX: let autograd know that there will be an additional reference to the tensor
1111             # that can be ignored when deciding whether to do gradient buffer inplacing.
1112             # Otherwise, inplacing could differ between tracing and subsequent execution.
1113             # For some models we tested this led to inputs no longer being in cudagraph pools,
1114             # leading to spurious re-recordings.
1115             # It also tells AMP cache that even though the tensor impls cannot be cached
1116             # in dtype conversions.
1117 
1118             torch._C._add_cached_tensor(out)
1119 
1120             self_ref = weakref.ref(self)
1121 
1122             # one reference in our array, and calling sys.getrefcount bumps the refcount by one
1123             def check_refcount(i):
1124                 return self_ref().get_output_refcount(i) == 2
1125 
1126             check = functools.partial(check_refcount, i=i)
1127 
1128             self.outputs_weakrefs[i] = StorageWeakRefWrapper(out, extra_ref_check=check)
1129             self.cached_tensor_outputs.append(out)

1153     def _is_cuda_graph_recorded_tensor(self, t: torch.Tensor):

1191     @staticmethod

1193         prev: List[List[bool]], curr: List[List[bool]]
1194     ) -> List[PathOutputIndex]:

1196         dead_indices = []

1199             assert len(outputs1) == len(outputs2)
1200             for j, (output1, output2) in enumerate(zip(outputs1, outputs2)):
1201                 if output1 != output2:

1348     def _allocate_and_copy_recording_inputs(self, inputs):
1349         """
1350         Allocate inputs for non static, non cudagraph managraphed managed tensors in the memory pool
1351         and copy over the tensor values.
1352         """
1353 
1354         torch.cuda.synchronize()
1355         self.stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
1356         recording_inputs = []
1357 
1358         with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True), torch.cuda.device(
1359             self.device
1360         ), _use_cuda_memory_pool_manager(
1361             self.device,
1362             mem_pool=self.cuda_graphs_pool,
1363             stream=self.stream,
1364         ):
1365             for i, inp in enumerate(inputs):
1366                 if i not in self.static_input_idxs:
1367                     # static_input does an allocation!
1368                     recording_inputs.append(static_input(inp))
1369                     # copy over and clear non recording input
1370                     self._copy_input(i, recording_inputs[-1], inp)
1371                     inputs[i] = None
1372                     del inp
1373                 else:
1374                     recording_inputs.append(inp)
1375 
1376         return recording_inputs

1378     def check_invariants(self, inputs: List[Tensor]) -> bool:
1379         """
1380         Checks if this node can be run. The same pattern of tensor liveness and tensors
1381         managed in the cudagraph private pool must remain stable.
1382         """
1383 
1384         # previously managed data pointers remain stable
1385         for idx in self.cudagraph_managed_idxs:
1386             if inputs[idx].data_ptr() != self.static_input_data_ptrs[idx]:
1387                 return False
1388 
1389         if not self._check_liveness(
1390             self.expected_dead_indices_before_graph, self.path_weakrefs
1391         ):
1392             return False
1393 
1394         # the cudagraph managed tensors which died upon recording must also die upon
1395         # this invocation. it is too late to check after we've replayed the graph,
1396         # because we would have already written over their memory.
1397         for idx in self.cudagraph_managed_idxs:
1398             inputs[idx] = None
1399 
1400         check(
1401             self._check_liveness(
1402                 self.expected_dead_indices_after_graph, self.path_weakrefs
1403             ),
1404             lambda: "TODO: graph recording observed an input tensor deallocate during graph "
1405             " recording that did not occur during replay. Please file an issue.",
1406         )
1407         return True

1419 def get_cudagraph_segments(pool_id):

1424 def get_block_addrs(pool_id, live_only=True):
1425     blocks = []
1426 
1427     for segment in get_cudagraph_segments(pool_id):
1428         addr = segment["address"]
1429         for block in segment["blocks"]:
1430             if block["state"] == "active_allocated" or not live_only:
1431                 blocks.append(addr)
1432 
1433             addr += block["size"]
1434 
1435     return blocks

1438 def format_tb(caching_allocator_trace):
1439     formatted_traceback = []
1440 
1441     MAX_LENGTH = 20
1442 
1443     for entry in caching_allocator_trace["frames"][0:MAX_LENGTH]:
1444         formatted_traceback.append(
1445             traceback.FrameSummary(entry["filename"], entry["line"], entry["name"])
1446         )

1451 def check_memory_pool(device, pool_id, live_storages_ptrs: List[StorageWeakRefWrapper]):
1452     assert all(
1453         isinstance(elem, StorageWeakRefWrapper) for elem in live_storages_ptrs
1454     )  # noqa: C419
1455     unique_storages = {stor.data_ptr() for stor in live_storages_ptrs if stor()}
1456 
1457     # check if there is a divergence first, then do the expensive snapshot call after
1458     # we know it will error
1459     if torch._C._cuda_checkPoolLiveAllocations(device, pool_id, unique_storages):
1460         return
1461 
1462     segments = get_cudagraph_segments(pool_id)
1463 
1464     allocated_not_in_live_storages = {}
1465 
1466     for segment in segments:
1467         addr = segment["address"]
1468         for block in segment["blocks"]:
1469             if block["state"] == "active_allocated":
1470                 if addr not in unique_storages:
1471                     allocated_not_in_live_storages[addr] = block
1472                 else:
1473                     unique_storages.remove(addr)
1474 
1475             addr += block["size"]
1476 
1477     check(
1478         len(unique_storages) == 0,
1479         lambda: f"These storage data ptrs are not allocated in pool {pool_id} but should be {unique_storages}",
1480     )
1481 
1482     if allocated_not_in_live_storages != 0:
1483         formatted = []
1484         for dp, block in allocated_not_in_live_storages.items():
1485             trace = (
1486                 format_tb(block["history"][-1]) if block.get("history", None) else None
1487             )
1488             formatted.append(f"Data Pointer: {dp}, history: \n{trace}")
1489         formatted_s = "\n".join(formatted)
1490         msg = (
1491             f"These live storage data ptrs are in the cudagraph pool but not "
1492             f"accounted for as an output of cudagraph trees: \n\n{formatted_s}"
1493         )
1494         raise RuntimeError(msg)

1515 class CUDAGraphTreeManager:
1516     """
1517     Groups individual recordings or executions of cuda graphs into a tree of recordings,
1518     and checks required invariants, and manages warmups of graphs.

1520     When graphs are recorded in the same tree, it enforces subsequent execution
1521     to follow the same order and have the same output tensor livespans. To remove
1522     unnecessary coupling of cuda graphs (and additional imposed invariants),
1523     the tree manager will end a currently recording tree whenever it is valid - when
1524     the memory pool no longer has any live allocations.

1527     Currently this is hardcoded `GenerationTracker.generation` tracked in torch dynamo.
1528     # TODO: make generation increment configurable, warn on overwrite.
1529 
1530     We run graph warmups in the cudagraph memory pool and return the result on the first invocation
1531     of a function. For many models it is important to reclaim activations as you run the backward.
1532     If we were to warm up the model and keep an extra copy of the inputs around to subsequently
1533     use for recording, we would incur a memory penalty. Additionally, if we are part way through training
1534     your model and need to recompile, memory will be allocated to the cuda graph pool, so we run this
1535     warmup run in the cuda graph memory pool. As for recording, warm up needs the state of live tensors
1536     to be accurately reflected so we checkpoint the allocator state if we need to warm up following graph
1537     replay.
1538     """

1544         # liveness would create a dependency.

1558         # will not be reused; separate recordings would have use the same memory pool, but not
1559         # the same memory.

1638     def _run(self, new_inputs: List[Tensor], function_id: FunctionID):

1650         # because both depend on the state of the caching allocator. if we warm up graph A,

import sys
import os
import argparse
import logging

from server.log.decorators import Log
from server.jim.utils import *
from server.core import MessageProcessor
from server.db_server import ServerDB
from server.server_gui.main_window import MainWindow
from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QApplication

logger = logging.getLogger('server_logger')
log = Log(logger)


@log
def arg_parser(default_port, default_address):
    """
    Парсер аргументов коммандной строки.
    :param default_port: Порт
    :param default_address: IP
    :return: Порт, IP, GUI-флаг
    """
    logger.debug(
        f'Инициализация парсера аргументов коммандной строки: {sys.argv}')
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('-p', default=default_port, type=int, nargs='?')
    parser.add_argument('-a', default=default_address, nargs='?')
    parser.add_argument('--no_gui', action='store_true')
    namespace = parser.parse_args(sys.argv[1:])
    listen_address = namespace.a
    listen_port = namespace.p
    gui_flag = namespace.no_gui
    logger.debug('Аргументы успешно загружены.')
    return listen_address, listen_port, gui_flag


@log
def config_load():
    """
    Парсер конфигурационного ini файла.
    :return: конфигия
    """
    config = configparser.ConfigParser()
    dir_path = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
    config.read(f"{dir_path}/{'server.ini'}")
    # Если конфиг файл загружен правильно, запускаемся, иначе конфиг по
    # умолчанию.
    if 'SETTINGS' in config:
        return config
    else:
        config.add_section('SETTINGS')
        config.set('SETTINGS', 'Default_port', str(DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT))
        config.set('SETTINGS', 'Listen_Address', '')
        config.set('SETTINGS', 'Database_path', '')
        config.set('SETTINGS', 'Database_file', 'server_database.db3')
        return config


@log
def main():
    """
    Основная функция
    :return: None
    """
    # Загрузка файла конфигурации сервера
    config = config_load()

    # Загрузка параметров командной строки, если нет параметров, то задаём
    # значения по умоланию.
    listen_address, listen_port, gui_flag = arg_parser(
        config['SETTINGS']['Default_port'], config['SETTINGS']['Listen_Address'])

    # Инициализация базы данных
    database = ServerDB(
        os.path.join(
            config['SETTINGS']['Database_path'],
            config['SETTINGS']['Database_file']))

    # Создание экземпляра класса - сервера и его запуск:
    server = MessageProcessor(listen_address, listen_port, database)
    server.daemon = True
    server.start()

    # Если  указан параметр без GUI то запускаем простенький обработчик
    # консольного ввода
    if gui_flag:
        while True:
            command = input('Введите exit для завершения работы сервера.')
            if command == 'exit':
                # Если выход, то завршаем основной цикл сервера.
                server.running = False
                server.join()
                break

    # Если не указан запуск без GUI, то запускаем GUI:
    else:
        # Создаём графическое окуружение для сервера:
        server_app = QApplication(sys.argv)
        server_app.setAttribute(Qt.AA_DisableWindowContextHelpButton)
        main_window = MainWindow(database, server, config)

        # Запускаем GUI
        server_app.exec_()

        # По закрытию окон останавливаем обработчик сообщений
        server.running = False


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Idiom 655 (use-requirement-markings-for-typed-dict)

Definition: Checks for cases where required or not required markings can be used to simplify TypedDict classes.

Rationale: Creation of multiple subclasses to accomodate optional keys in TypedDict with a base class containing required keys leads to inefficient design and duplicated code that negatively impacts maintainability.

Example:
class _MovieBase(TypedDict):  # implicitly total=True
    title: str

class Movie(_MovieBase, total=False):
    year: int

class Movie(TypedDict):
    title: str
    year: NotRequired[int]

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import requests
from pyld import jsonld
import json

# Our endpoints
INVENTARIS = 'https://inventaris.onroerenderfgoed.be'
AFBEELDINGEN = 'https://beeldbank.onroerenderfgoed.be/images'
ERFGOEDOBJECTEN = INVENTARIS + '/erfgoedobjecten'
AANDUIDINGSOBJECTEN = INVENTARIS + '/aanduidingsobjecten'
THEMAS = INVENTARIS + '/themas'

def get_data(url, parameters):
    '''
    Fetch all data from a url until there are no more `next` urls in the Link
    header.

    :param str url: The url to fetch from
    :param dict parameters: A dict of query string parameters
    :rtype: dict
    '''
    data = []

    headers = {'Accept': 'application/json'}

    res = requests.get(url, params=parameters, headers=headers)

    data.extend(res.json())

    while 'next' in res.links:
        res = requests.get(res.links['next']['url'], headers=headers)
        data.extend(res.json())

    return data

def add_type(collection, rtype):
    """
    Add the resource type to a resource

    :param list collection: Collection of resources to add a type to
    :param str rtype: The type of all resources in this collection
    :rtype: list
    """
    for c in collection:
        c.update({'@type': rtype})

def add_locatie_samenvatting(afbeeldingen):
    """
    Summarize the location of an image

    :param list afbeeldingen: Collection of afbeeldingen to summarize
    :rtype: list
    """
    for a in afbeeldingen:
        s = ''
        hnr = a.get('location', {}).get('housenumber', {}).get('name')
        straat = a.get('location', {}).get('street', {}).get('name')
        gemeente = a.get('location', {}).get('municipality', {}).get('name')
        prov = a.get('location', {}).get('province', {}).get('name')
        if straat and hnr:
            s = '{} {} ({})'.format(straat, hnr, gemeente)
        elif straat:
            s = '{} ({})'.format(straat, gemeente)
        else:
            s = '{} ({})'.format(gemeente, prov)
        a.update({'locatie_samenvatting': s})

# Determine the CRAB ID for the gemeente you want
# https://loc.geopunt.be/v4/Location?q=knokke-heist
MUNICIPALITY_ID = 191

# Fetch all data
afbeeldingen = get_data(AFBEELDINGEN, {'municipality': MUNICIPALITY_ID})
erfgoedobjecten = get_data(ERFGOEDOBJECTEN, {'gemeente': MUNICIPALITY_ID})
aanduidingsobjecten = get_data(AANDUIDINGSOBJECTEN, {'gemeente': MUNICIPALITY_ID})
themas = get_data(THEMAS, {'gemeente': MUNICIPALITY_ID})

# Add everything together and transform to linked data
inventaris_context = {
    "dct": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/",
    "naam": "dct:title",
    "korte_beschrijving": "dct:description",
    "locatie_samenvatting": "dct:spatial",
    "uri": "@id",
    "Thema": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Thema",
    "Erfgoedobject": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Erfgoedobject",
    "Aanduidingsobject": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Aanduidingsobject"
}
beeldbank_context = {
    "dct": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/",
    "title": "dct:title",
    "description": "dct:description",
    "locatie_samenvatting": "dct:spatial",
    "uri": "@id",
    "Afbeelding": "https://purl.org/dc/dcmiType/Image"
}

# Add types to all datasets and location summary to images
add_type(erfgoedobjecten, "Erfgoedobject")
erfgoedobjecten = jsonld.expand(erfgoedobjecten, {'expandContext':inventaris_context})
add_type(aanduidingsobjecten, "Aanduidingsobject")
aanduidingsobjecten = jsonld.expand(aanduidingsobjecten, {'expandContext':inventaris_context})
add_type(themas, "Thema")
themas = jsonld.expand(themas, {'expandContext':inventaris_context})
add_type(afbeeldingen, "Afbeelding")
add_locatie_samenvatting(afbeeldingen)
afbeeldingen = jsonld.expand(afbeeldingen, {'expandContext':beeldbank_context})

# Add all datasets together
stuff = erfgoedobjecten + aanduidingsobjecten + themas + afbeeldingen

# Compact all data to simplify the keys we're working with
dct_context = {
    "dct": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/",
    "title": "dct:title",
    "description": "dct:description",
    "spatial": "dct:spatial",
    "uri": "@id",
    "type": "@type",
    "Thema": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Thema",
    "Erfgoedobject": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Erfgoedobject",
    "Aanduidingsobject": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Aanduidingsobject",
    "Afbeelding": "https://purl.org/dc/dcmiType/Image"
}
compactstuff = jsonld.compact(stuff, dct_context)

# Print all records to the screen
for s in compactstuff['@graph']:
    h = '{}'.format(s['title'])
    print(h)
    print(len(h)*'=')
    print('Type: {}'.format(s['type']))
    print('URI: {}'.format(s['uri']))
    print('Location: {}'.format(s['spatial']))
    if 'description' in s and s['description']:
        print(s['description'])
    print()

import requests
from pyld import jsonld
import json

# Our endpoints
INVENTARIS = 'https://inventaris.onroerenderfgoed.be'
AFBEELDINGEN = 'https://beeldbank.onroerenderfgoed.be/images'
ERFGOEDOBJECTEN = INVENTARIS + '/erfgoedobjecten'
AANDUIDINGSOBJECTEN = INVENTARIS + '/aanduidingsobjecten'
THEMAS = INVENTARIS + '/themas'

def get_data(url, parameters):
    '''
    Fetch all data from a url until there are no more `next` urls in the Link
    header.

    :param str url: The url to fetch from
    :param dict parameters: A dict of query string parameters
    :rtype: dict
    '''
    data = []

    headers = {'Accept': 'application/json'}

    res = requests.get(url, params=parameters, headers=headers)

    data.extend(res.json())

    while 'next' in res.links:
        res = requests.get(res.links['next']['url'], headers=headers)
        data.extend(res.json())

    return data

def add_type(collection, rtype):
    """
    Add the resource type to a resource

    :param list collection: Collection of resources to add a type to
    :param str rtype: The type of all resources in this collection
    :rtype: list
    """
    for c in collection:
        c.update({'@type': rtype})

def add_locatie_samenvatting(afbeeldingen):
    """
    Summarize the location of an image

    :param list afbeeldingen: Collection of afbeeldingen to summarize
    :rtype: list
    """
    for a in afbeeldingen:
        s = ''
        hnr = a.get('location', {}).get('housenumber', {}).get('name')
        straat = a.get('location', {}).get('street', {}).get('name')
        gemeente = a.get('location', {}).get('municipality', {}).get('name')
        prov = a.get('location', {}).get('province', {}).get('name')
        if straat and hnr:
            s = '{} {} ({})'.format(straat, hnr, gemeente)
        elif straat:
            s = '{} ({})'.format(straat, gemeente)
        else:
            s = '{} ({})'.format(gemeente, prov)
        a.update({'locatie_samenvatting': s})

# Determine the CRAB ID for the gemeente you want
# https://loc.geopunt.be/v4/Location?q=knokke-heist
MUNICIPALITY_ID = 191

# Fetch all data
afbeeldingen = get_data(AFBEELDINGEN, {'municipality': MUNICIPALITY_ID})
erfgoedobjecten = get_data(ERFGOEDOBJECTEN, {'gemeente': MUNICIPALITY_ID})
aanduidingsobjecten = get_data(AANDUIDINGSOBJECTEN, {'gemeente': MUNICIPALITY_ID})
themas = get_data(THEMAS, {'gemeente': MUNICIPALITY_ID})

# Add everything together and transform to linked data
inventaris_context = {
    "dct": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/",
    "naam": "dct:title",
    "korte_beschrijving": "dct:description",
    "locatie_samenvatting": "dct:spatial",
    "uri": "@id",
    "Thema": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Thema",
    "Erfgoedobject": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Erfgoedobject",
    "Aanduidingsobject": "https://id.erfgoed.net/vocab/ontology#Aanduidingsobject"
}
beeldbank_context = {
    "dct": "http://purl.org/dc/terms/",
    "title": "dct:title",
    "description": "dct:description",
    "locatie_samenvatting": "dct:spatial",
    "uri": "@id",
    "Afbeelding": "https://purl.org/dc/dcmiType/Image"
}

# Add types to all datasets and location summary to images
add_type(erfgoedobjecten, "Erfgoedobject")
erfgoedobjecten = jsonld.expand(erfgoedobjecten, {'expandContext':inventaris_context})
add_type(aanduidingsobjecten, "Aanduidingsobject")
aanduidingsobjecten = jsonld.expand(aanduidingsobjecten, {'expandContext':inventaris_context})
add_type(themas, "Thema")
themas = jsonld.expand(themas, {'expandContext':inventaris_context})
add_type(afbeeldingen, "Afbeelding")
add_locatie_samenvatting(afbeeldingen)
afbeeldingen = jsonld.expand(afbeeldingen, {'expandContext':beeldbank_context})

# Add all datasets together

from asyncio import Queue, create_task

from aiodocker import Docker
from aiodocker.containers import DockerContainer


class Monitor:
	queue: Queue

	def __init__(self):
		self.queue = Queue()

		create_task(self.query_running())
		create_task(self.query_started())

	async def query_running(self) -> None:
		containers = await Docker().containers.list()
		for container in containers:
			await container.show()
			await self.handle(container)

	async def query_started(self) -> None:
		channel = Docker().events.subscribe()
		while channel:
			event = await channel.get()
			if event['Type'] == 'container' and event['status'] == 'start':
				container = Docker().containers.container(event['id'])
				await container.show()
				await self.handle(container)

	async def handle(self, container: DockerContainer) -> None:
		try:
			await self.queue.put((
				container['Config']['Labels']['domain'],
				next(iter(container['NetworkSettings']['Networks'].values()))['IPAddress'],
			))
		except KeyError:
			pass

	def __aiter__(self):
		return self

	async def __anext__(self):
		return await self.queue.get()

        .. versionadded:: 1.1

        .. seealso::

            :ref:`lateral_selects` -  overview of usage.

        """
        return Lateral(self, name)

    def tablesample(self, sampling, name=None, seed=None):
        """Return a TABLESAMPLE alias of this :class:`.FromClause`.

        The return value is the :class:`.TableSample` construct also
        provided by the top-level :func:`~.expression.tablesample` function.

        .. versionadded:: 1.1

        .. seealso::

            :func:`~.expression.tablesample` - usage guidelines and parameters

        """
        return TableSample(self, sampling, name, seed)

    def is_derived_from(self, fromclause):
        """Return True if this FromClause is 'derived' from the given
        FromClause.

        An example would be an Alias of a Table is derived from that Table.

        """
        # this is essentially an "identity" check in the base class.
        # Other constructs override this to traverse through
        # contained elements.
        return fromclause in self._cloned_set

    def _is_lexical_equivalent(self, other):
        """Return True if this FromClause and the other represent
        the same lexical identity.

        This tests if either one is a copy of the other, or
        if they are the same via annotation identity.

        """
        return self._cloned_set.intersection(other._cloned_set)

    @util.dependencies("sqlalchemy.sql.util")
    def replace_selectable(self, sqlutil, old, alias):
        """replace all occurrences of FromClause 'old' with the given Alias
        object, returning a copy of this :class:`.FromClause`.

        """

        return sqlutil.ClauseAdapter(alias).traverse(self)

    def correspond_on_equivalents(self, column, equivalents):
        """Return corresponding_column for the given column, or if None
        search for a match in the given dictionary.

        """
        col = self.corresponding_column(column, require_embedded=True)
        if col is None and col in equivalents:
            for equiv in equivalents[col]:
                nc = self.corresponding_column(equiv, require_embedded=True)
                if nc:
                    return nc
        return col

    def corresponding_column(self, column, require_embedded=False):
        """Given a :class:`.ColumnElement`, return the exported
        :class:`.ColumnElement` object from this :class:`.Selectable`
        which corresponds to that original
        :class:`~sqlalchemy.schema.Column` via a common ancestor
        column.

        :param column: the target :class:`.ColumnElement` to be matched

        :param require_embedded: only return corresponding columns for
         the given :class:`.ColumnElement`, if the given
         :class:`.ColumnElement` is actually present within a sub-element
         of this :class:`.FromClause`.  Normally the column will match if
         it merely shares a common ancestor with one of the exported
         columns of this :class:`.FromClause`.

        """

        def embedded(expanded_proxy_set, target_set):
            for t in target_set.difference(expanded_proxy_set):
                if not set(_expand_cloned([t])
                           ).intersection(expanded_proxy_set):
                    return False
            return True

        # don't dig around if the column is locally present
        if self.c.contains_column(column):
            return column
        col, intersect = None, None
        target_set = column.proxy_set
        cols = self.c._all_columns
        for c in cols:
            expanded_proxy_set = set(_expand_cloned(c.proxy_set))
            i = target_set.intersection(expanded_proxy_set)
            if i and (not require_embedded
                      or embedded(expanded_proxy_set, target_set)):
                if col is None:

                    # no corresponding column yet, pick this one.

                    col, intersect = c, i
                elif len(i) > len(intersect):

                    # 'c' has a larger field of correspondence than
                    # 'col'. i.e. selectable.c.a1_x->a1.c.x->table.c.x
                    # matches a1.c.x->table.c.x better than
                    # selectable.c.x->table.c.x does.

                    col, intersect = c, i
                elif i == intersect:

                    # they have the same field of correspondence. see
                    # which proxy_set has fewer columns in it, which
                    # indicates a closer relationship with the root
                    # column. Also take into account the "weight"
                    # attribute which CompoundSelect() uses to give
                    # higher precedence to columns based on vertical
                    # position in the compound statement, and discard
                    # columns that have no reference to the target
                    # column (also occurs with CompoundSelect)

                    col_distance = util.reduce(
                        operator.add,
                        [sc._annotations.get('weight', 1) for sc in
                         col.proxy_set if sc.shares_lineage(column)])
                    c_distance = util.reduce(
                        operator.add,
                        [sc._annotations.get('weight', 1) for sc in
                         c.proxy_set if sc.shares_lineage(column)])
                    if c_distance < col_distance:
                        col, intersect = c, i
        return col

    @property
    def description(self):
        """a brief description of this FromClause.

        Used primarily for error message formatting.

        """
        return getattr(self, 'name', self.__class__.__name__ + " object")

    def _reset_exported(self):
        """delete memoized collections when a FromClause is cloned."""

        self._memoized_property.expire_instance(self)

    @_memoized_property
    def columns(self):
        """A named-based collection of :class:`.ColumnElement` objects
        maintained by this :class:`.FromClause`.

        The :attr:`.columns`, or :attr:`.c` collection, is the gateway
        to the construction of SQL expressions using table-bound or
        other selectable-bound columns::

            select([mytable]).where(mytable.c.somecolumn == 1)

        """

        if '_columns' not in self.__dict__:
            self._init_collections()
            self._populate_column_collection()
        return self._columns.as_immutable()

    @_memoized_property
    def primary_key(self):
        """Return the collection of Column objects which comprise the
        primary key of this FromClause."""

        self._init_collections()
        self._populate_column_collection()
        return self.primary_key

    @_memoized_property
    def foreign_keys(self):
        """Return the collection of ForeignKey objects which this
        FromClause references."""

        self._init_collections()
        self._populate_column_collection()
        return self.foreign_keys

    c = property(attrgetter('columns'),
                 doc="An alias for the :attr:`.columns` attribute.")
    _select_iterable = property(attrgetter('columns'))

    def _init_collections(self):
        assert '_columns' not in self.__dict__
        assert 'primary_key' not in self.__dict__
        assert 'foreign_keys' not in self.__dict__

        self._columns = ColumnCollection()
        self.primary_key = ColumnSet()
        self.foreign_keys = set()

    @property
    def _cols_populated(self):
        return '_columns' in self.__dict__

    def _populate_column_collection(self):
        """Called on subclasses to establish the .c collection.

        Each implementation has a different way of establishing
        this collection.

        """

    def _refresh_for_new_column(self, column):
        """Given a column added to the .c collection of an underlying
        selectable, produce the local version of that column, assuming this
        selectable ultimately should proxy this column.

        this is used to "ping" a derived selectable to add a new column
        to its .c. collection when a Column has been added to one of the
        Table objects it ultimtely derives from.

        If the given selectable hasn't populated its .c. collection yet,
        it should at least pass on the message to the contained selectables,
        but it will return None.

        This method is currently used by Declarative to allow Table
        columns to be added to a partially constructed inheritance
        mapping that may have already produced joins.  The method
        isn't public right now, as the full span of implications
        and/or caveats aren't yet clear.

        It's also possible that this functionality could be invoked by
        default via an event, which would require that
        selectables maintain a weak referencing collection of all
        derivations.

        """
        if not self._cols_populated:
            return None
        elif (column.key in self.columns and
              self.columns[column.key] is column):
            return column
        else:
            return None


class Join(FromClause):
    """represent a ``JOIN`` construct between two :class:`.FromClause`
    elements.

    The public constructor function for :class:`.Join` is the module-level
    :func:`.join()` function, as well as the :meth:`.FromClause.join` method
    of any :class:`.FromClause` (e.g. such as :class:`.Table`).

    .. seealso::

        :func:`.join`

        :meth:`.FromClause.join`

    """
    __visit_name__ = 'join'

    _is_join = True

    def __init__(self, left, right, onclause=None, isouter=False, full=False):
        """Construct a new :class:`.Join`.

        The usual entrypoint here is the :func:`~.expression.join`
        function or the :meth:`.FromClause.join` method of any
        :class:`.FromClause` object.

        """
        self.left = _interpret_as_from(left)
        self.right = _interpret_as_from(right).self_group()

        if onclause is None:
            self.onclause = self._match_primaries(self.left, self.right)
        else:
            self.onclause = onclause

        self.isouter = isouter
        self.full = full

    @classmethod
    def _create_outerjoin(cls, left, right, onclause=None, full=False):
        """Return an ``OUTER JOIN`` clause element.

        The returned object is an instance of :class:`.Join`.

        Similar functionality is also available via the
        :meth:`~.FromClause.outerjoin()` method on any
        :class:`.FromClause`.

        :param left: The left side of the join.

        :param right: The right side of the join.

        :param onclause:  Optional criterion for the ``ON`` clause, is
          derived from foreign key relationships established between
          left and right otherwise.

        To chain joins together, use the :meth:`.FromClause.join` or
        :meth:`.FromClause.outerjoin` methods on the resulting
        :class:`.Join` object.

        """
        return cls(left, right, onclause, isouter=True, full=full)

    @classmethod
    def _create_join(cls, left, right, onclause=None, isouter=False,
                     full=False):
        """Produce a :class:`.Join` object, given two :class:`.FromClause`
        expressions.

        E.g.::

            j = join(user_table, address_table,
                     user_table.c.id == address_table.c.user_id)
            stmt = select([user_table]).select_from(j)

        would emit SQL along the lines of::

            SELECT user.id, user.name FROM user
            JOIN address ON user.id = address.user_id

        Similar functionality is available given any
        :class:`.FromClause` object (e.g. such as a :class:`.Table`) using
        the :meth:`.FromClause.join` method.

        :param left: The left side of the join.

        :param right: the right side of the join; this is any
         :class:`.FromClause` object such as a :class:`.Table` object, and
         may also be a selectable-compatible object such as an ORM-mapped
         class.

        :param onclause: a SQL expression representing the ON clause of the
         join.  If left at ``None``, :meth:`.FromClause.join` will attempt to
         join the two tables based on a foreign key relationship.

        :param isouter: if True, render a LEFT OUTER JOIN, instead of JOIN.

        :param full: if True, render a FULL OUTER JOIN, instead of JOIN.

         .. versionadded:: 1.1

        .. seealso::

            :meth:`.FromClause.join` - method form, based on a given left side

            :class:`.Join` - the type of object produced

        """

        return cls(left, right, onclause, isouter, full)

    @property
    def description(self):
        return "Join object on %s(%d) and %s(%d)" % (
            self.left.description,
            id(self.left),
            self.right.description,
            id(self.right))

    def is_derived_from(self, fromclause):
        return fromclause is self or \
            self.left.is_derived_from(fromclause) or \
            self.right.is_derived_from(fromclause)

    def self_group(self, against=None):
        return FromGrouping(self)

    @util.dependencies("sqlalchemy.sql.util")
    def _populate_column_collection(self, sqlutil):
        columns = [c for c in self.left.columns] + \
            [c for c in self.right.columns]

        self.primary_key.extend(sqlutil.reduce_columns(
            (c for c in columns if c.primary_key), self.onclause))
        self._columns.update((col._label, col) for col in columns)
        self.foreign_keys.update(itertools.chain(
            *[col.foreign_keys for col in columns]))

    def _refresh_for_new_column(self, column):
        col = self.left._refresh_for_new_column(column)
        if col is None:
            col = self.right._refresh_for_new_column(column)
        if col is not None:
            if self._cols_populated:
                self._columns[col._label] = col
                self.foreign_keys.update(col.foreign_keys)
                if col.primary_key:
                    self.primary_key.add(col)
                return col
        return None

    def _copy_internals(self, clone=_clone, **kw):
        self._reset_exported()
        self.left = clone(self.left, **kw)
        self.right = clone(self.right, **kw)
        self.onclause = clone(self.onclause, **kw)

    def get_children(self, **kwargs):
        return self.left, self.right, self.onclause

    def _match_primaries(self, left, right):
        if isinstance(left, Join):
            left_right = left.right
        else:
            left_right = None
        return self._join_condition(left, right, a_subset=left_right)

    @classmethod
    def _join_condition(cls, a, b, ignore_nonexistent_tables=False,
                                a_subset=None,
                                consider_as_foreign_keys=None):
        """create a join condition between two tables or selectables.

        e.g.::

            join_condition(tablea, tableb)

        would produce an expression along the lines of::

            tablea.c.id==tableb.c.tablea_id

        The join is determined based on the foreign key relationships
        between the two selectables.   If there are multiple ways
        to join, or no way to join, an error is raised.

        :param ignore_nonexistent_tables:  Deprecated - this
        flag is no longer used.  Only resolution errors regarding
        the two given tables are propagated.

        :param a_subset: An optional expression that is a sub-component
        of ``a``.  An attempt will be made to join to just this sub-component
        first before looking at the full ``a`` construct, and if found
        will be successful even if there are other ways to join to ``a``.
        This allows the "right side" of a join to be passed thereby
        providing a "natural join".

        """
        constraints = cls._joincond_scan_left_right(
            a, a_subset, b, consider_as_foreign_keys)

        if len(constraints) > 1:
            cls._joincond_trim_constraints(
                a, b, constraints, consider_as_foreign_keys)

        if len(constraints) == 0:
            if isinstance(b, FromGrouping):
                hint = " Perhaps you meant to convert the right side to a "\
                    "subquery using alias()?"
            else:
                hint = ""
            raise exc.NoForeignKeysError(
                "Can't find any foreign key relationships "
                "between '%s' and '%s'.%s" %
                (a.description, b.description, hint))

        crit = [(x == y) for x, y in list(constraints.values())[0]]
        if len(crit) == 1:
            return (crit[0])
        else:
            return and_(*crit)

    @classmethod
    def _joincond_scan_left_right(
            cls, a, a_subset, b, consider_as_foreign_keys):
        constraints = collections.defaultdict(list)

        for left in (a_subset, a):
            if left is None:
                continue
            for fk in sorted(
                    b.foreign_keys,
                    key=lambda fk: fk.parent._creation_order):
                if consider_as_foreign_keys is not None and \
                        fk.parent not in consider_as_foreign_keys:
                    continue
                try:
                    col = fk.get_referent(left)
                except exc.NoReferenceError as nrte:
                    if nrte.table_name == left.name:
                        raise
                    else:
                        continue

                if col is not None:
                    constraints[fk.constraint].append((col, fk.parent))
            if left is not b:
                for fk in sorted(
                        left.foreign_keys,
                        key=lambda fk: fk.parent._creation_order):
                    if consider_as_foreign_keys is not None and \
                            fk.parent not in consider_as_foreign_keys:
                        continue
                    try:
                        col = fk.get_referent(b)
                    except exc.NoReferenceError as nrte:
                        if nrte.table_name == b.name:
                            raise
                        else:
                            continue

                    if col is not None:
                        constraints[fk.constraint].append((col, fk.parent))
            if constraints:
                break
        return constraints

    @classmethod
    def _joincond_trim_constraints(
            cls, a, b, constraints, consider_as_foreign_keys):
        # more than one constraint matched.  narrow down the list
        # to include just those FKCs that match exactly to
        # "consider_as_foreign_keys".
        if consider_as_foreign_keys:
            for const in list(constraints):
                if set(f.parent for f in const.elements) != set(
                        consider_as_foreign_keys):
                    del constraints[const]

        # if still multiple constraints, but
        # they all refer to the exact same end result, use it.
        if len(constraints) > 1:
            dedupe = set(tuple(crit) for crit in constraints.values())
            if len(dedupe) == 1:
                key = list(constraints)[0]
                constraints = {key: constraints[key]}

        if len(constraints) != 1:
            raise exc.AmbiguousForeignKeysError(
                "Can't determine join between '%s' and '%s'; "
                "tables have more than one foreign key "
                "constraint relationship between them. "
                "Please specify the 'onclause' of this "
                "join explicitly." % (a.description, b.description))

    def select(self, whereclause=None, **kwargs):
        r"""Create a :class:`.Select` from this :class:`.Join`.

        The equivalent long-hand form, given a :class:`.Join` object
        ``j``, is::

            from sqlalchemy import select
            j = select([j.left, j.right], **kw).\
                        where(whereclause).\
                        select_from(j)

        :param whereclause: the WHERE criterion that will be sent to
          the :func:`select()` function

        :param \**kwargs: all other kwargs are sent to the
          underlying :func:`select()` function.

        """
        collist = [self.left, self.right]

        return Select(collist, whereclause, from_obj=[self], **kwargs)

    @property
    def bind(self):
        return self.left.bind or self.right.bind

    @util.dependencies("sqlalchemy.sql.util")
    def alias(self, sqlutil, name=None, flat=False):
        r"""return an alias of this :class:`.Join`.

        The default behavior here is to first produce a SELECT
        construct from this :class:`.Join`, then to produce an
        :class:`.Alias` from that.  So given a join of the form::

            j = table_a.join(table_b, table_a.c.id == table_b.c.a_id)

        The JOIN by itself would look like::

            table_a JOIN table_b ON table_a.id = table_b.a_id

        Whereas the alias of the above, ``j.alias()``, would in a
        SELECT context look like::

            (SELECT table_a.id AS table_a_id, table_b.id AS table_b_id,
                table_b.a_id AS table_b_a_id
                FROM table_a
                JOIN table_b ON table_a.id = table_b.a_id) AS anon_1

        The equivalent long-hand form, given a :class:`.Join` object
        ``j``, is::

            from sqlalchemy import select, alias
            j = alias(
                select([j.left, j.right]).\
                    select_from(j).\
                    with_labels(True).\
                    correlate(False),
                name=name
            )

        The selectable produced by :meth:`.Join.alias` features the same
        columns as that of the two individual selectables presented under
        a single name - the individual columns are "auto-labeled", meaning
        the ``.c.`` collection of the resulting :class:`.Alias` represents
        the names of the individual columns using a
        ``<tablename>_<columname>`` scheme::

            j.c.table_a_id
            j.c.table_b_a_id

        :meth:`.Join.alias` also features an alternate
        option for aliasing joins which produces no enclosing SELECT and
        does not normally apply labels to the column names.  The
        ``flat=True`` option will call :meth:`.FromClause.alias`
        against the left and right sides individually.
        Using this option, no new ``SELECT`` is produced;
        we instead, from a construct as below::

            j = table_a.join(table_b, table_a.c.id == table_b.c.a_id)
            j = j.alias(flat=True)

        we get a result like this::

            table_a AS table_a_1 JOIN table_b AS table_b_1 ON
            table_a_1.id = table_b_1.a_id

        The ``flat=True`` argument is also propagated to the contained
        selectables, so that a composite join such as::

            j = table_a.join(
                    table_b.join(table_c,
                            table_b.c.id == table_c.c.b_id),
                    table_b.c.a_id == table_a.c.id
                ).alias(flat=True)

        Will produce an expression like::

            table_a AS table_a_1 JOIN (
                    table_b AS table_b_1 JOIN table_c AS table_c_1
                    ON table_b_1.id = table_c_1.b_id
            ) ON table_a_1.id = table_b_1.a_id

        The standalone :func:`~.expression.alias` function as well as the
        base :meth:`.FromClause.alias` method also support the ``flat=True``
        argument as a no-op, so that the argument can be passed to the
        ``alias()`` method of any selectable.

        .. versionadded:: 0.9.0 Added the ``flat=True`` option to create
          "aliases" of joins without enclosing inside of a SELECT
          subquery.

        :param name: name given to the alias.

        :param flat: if True, produce an alias of the left and right
         sides of this :class:`.Join` and return the join of those
         two selectables.   This produces join expression that does not
         include an enclosing SELECT.

         .. versionadded:: 0.9.0

        .. seealso::

            :func:`~.expression.alias`

        """
        if flat:
            assert name is None, "Can't send name argument with flat"
            left_a, right_a = self.left.alias(flat=True), \
                self.right.alias(flat=True)
            adapter = sqlutil.ClauseAdapter(left_a).\
                chain(sqlutil.ClauseAdapter(right_a))

            return left_a.join(right_a, adapter.traverse(self.onclause),
                               isouter=self.isouter, full=self.full)
        else:
            return self.select(use_labels=True, correlate=False).alias(name)

    @property
    def _hide_froms(self):
        return itertools.chain(*[_from_objects(x.left, x.right)
                                 for x in self._cloned_set])

    @property
    def _from_objects(self):
        return [self] + \
            self.onclause._from_objects + \
            self.left._from_objects + \
            self.right._from_objects


class Alias(FromClause):
    """Represents an table or selectable alias (AS).

    Represents an alias, as typically applied to any table or
    sub-select within a SQL statement using the ``AS`` keyword (or
    without the keyword on certain databases such as Oracle).

    This object is constructed from the :func:`~.expression.alias` module
    level function as well as the :meth:`.FromClause.alias` method available
    on all :class:`.FromClause` subclasses.

    """

    __visit_name__ = 'alias'
    named_with_column = True

    _is_from_container = True

    def __init__(self, selectable, name=None):
        baseselectable = selectable
        while isinstance(baseselectable, Alias):
            baseselectable = baseselectable.element
        self.original = baseselectable
        self.supports_execution = baseselectable.supports_execution
        if self.supports_execution:
            self._execution_options = baseselectable._execution_options
        self.element = selectable
        if name is None:
            if self.original.named_with_column:
                name = getattr(self.original, 'name', None)
            name = _anonymous_label('%%(%d %s)s' % (id(self), name
                                                    or 'anon'))
        self.name = name

    def self_group(self, against=None):
        if isinstance(against, CompoundSelect) and \
            isinstance(self.original, Select) and \
                self.original._needs_parens_for_grouping():
            return FromGrouping(self)

        return super(Alias, self).self_group(against=against)

    @property
    def description(self):
        if util.py3k:
            return self.name
        else:
            return self.name.encode('ascii', 'backslashreplace')

    def as_scalar(self):
        try:
            return self.element.as_scalar()
        except AttributeError:
            raise AttributeError("Element %s does not support "
                                 "'as_scalar()'" % self.element)

    def is_derived_from(self, fromclause):
        if fromclause in self._cloned_set:
            return True
        return self.element.is_derived_from(fromclause)

    def _populate_column_collection(self):
        for col in self.element.columns._all_columns:
            col._make_proxy(self)

    def _refresh_for_new_column(self, column):
        col = self.element._refresh_for_new_column(column)
        if col is not None:
            if not self._cols_populated:
                return None
            else:
                return col._make_proxy(self)
        else:
            return None

    def _copy_internals(self, clone=_clone, **kw):
        # don't apply anything to an aliased Table
        # for now.   May want to drive this from
        # the given **kw.
        if isinstance(self.element, TableClause):
            return
        self._reset_exported()
        self.element = clone(self.element, **kw)
        baseselectable = self.element
        while isinstance(baseselectable, Alias):
            baseselectable = baseselectable.element
        self.original = baseselectable

    def get_children(self, column_collections=True, **kw):
        if column_collections:
            for c in self.c:
                yield c
        yield self.element

    @property
    def _from_objects(self):
        return [self]

    @property
    def bind(self):
        return self.element.bind


class Lateral(Alias):
    """Represent a LATERAL subquery.

    This object is constructed from the :func:`~.expression.lateral` module
    level function as well as the :meth:`.FromClause.lateral` method available
    on all :class:`.FromClause` subclasses.

    While LATERAL is part of the SQL standard, curently only more recent
    PostgreSQL versions provide support for this keyword.

    .. versionadded:: 1.1

    .. seealso::

        :ref:`lateral_selects` -  overview of usage.

    """

    __visit_name__ = 'lateral'


class TableSample(Alias):
    """Represent a TABLESAMPLE clause.

    This object is constructed from the :func:`~.expression.tablesample` module
    level function as well as the :meth:`.FromClause.tablesample` method available
    on all :class:`.FromClause` subclasses.

    .. versionadded:: 1.1

    .. seealso::

        :func:`~.expression.tablesample`

    """

    __visit_name__ = 'tablesample'

    def __init__(self, selectable, sampling,
                 name=None,
                 seed=None):
        self.sampling = sampling
        self.seed = seed
        super(TableSample, self).__init__(selectable, name=name)

    @util.dependencies("sqlalchemy.sql.functions")
    def _get_method(self, functions):
