480 class CUDAWarmupNode:
481     """
482     Simplified Wrapper around A CUDA Model that wraps outputs in storage refs and exposes
483     apis to get the live storages in the current chain of warmup.
484 
485     A CUDAWarmupNode may have either CUDAGraphNode or CUDAWarmupNode as a parent, but may only have
486     CUDAWarmupNode as children, because we cannot record or execute with tensors which do not have stable
487     memory addresses.
488 
489     CUDAWarmupNode and CUDAGraphNode have a number of differences that make it easier to use separate classes.
490     - Much of the CUDAGraphNode logic & initialization is based on the tensor properties of first recording. In the
491     first instance of warmup, these are not finalized yet.
492     - All Inputs to the RecordedFunction must be copied over to the cuda graph memory pool, this is unnecessary in warmup.
493     - CUDAWarmup is only used once and so does not need to optimize as much bookkeeping. It is much simpler.
494 
495     NB: this class and CUDAGraphNode need to expose `path_live_weakrefs`, `all_outputs_are_dead`, and
496     `self.outputs_weakrefs` for compatibility.
497     """
498 
499     def __init__(
500         self,
501         wrapped_function: WrappedFunction,
502         parent,
503         cuda_graphs_pool: Tuple[int, int],
504         existing_cuda_graph: torch.cuda.Graph,
505         device_index: int,
506         stack_traces: Optional[StackTraces],
507         stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
508         already_warm: bool,
509     ):
510         self.wrapped_function = wrapped_function
511         self.parent = parent
512         self.cuda_graphs_pool = cuda_graphs_pool
513         self.outputs_weakrefs: List[Optional[StorageWeakRefWrapper]] = []
514         self.existing_cuda_graph = existing_cuda_graph
515         self.has_run = False
516         self.device_index = device_index
517         self.stack_traces = stack_traces
518         self.stream = stream
519         self.already_warm = already_warm
520 
521     def run(self, new_inputs):
522         assert not self.has_run, "Wrapped function should never be run twice"
523 
524         # See: output_is_alias_of_persistent_static_inputs below. We should only be returning freshly created
525         # storages in path_live_weakrefs.
526         existing_path_data_ptrs = {
527             t.data_ptr() for t in self.path_live_weakrefs() if t()
528         }
529         non_cudagraph_inps = set()
530         for i in range(len(new_inputs)):
531             if (
532                 new_inputs[i].untyped_storage().data_ptr()
533                 not in existing_path_data_ptrs
534             ):
535                 non_cudagraph_inps.add(new_inputs[i].untyped_storage().data_ptr())
536 
537         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts and not self.already_warm:
538             refs = list(self.path_live_weakrefs())
539             check_memory_pool(self.device_index, self.cuda_graphs_pool, refs)
540 
541         with torch.cuda.device(
542             self.device_index
543         ), clear_cublas_manager(), _use_cuda_memory_pool_manager(
544             self.device_index, self.cuda_graphs_pool, self.stream
545         ), get_history_recording():
546             out = self.wrapped_function.model(new_inputs)
547 
548         # sync up stream used in `_use_cuda_memory_pool_manager` - TODO - wait stream instead ?
549         torch.cuda.synchronize()
550 
551         assert len(new_inputs) == 0
552 
553         self.outputs_weakrefs.extend(
554             [
555                 map_to_ref(o)
556                 for o in out
557                 if o is not None
558                 and o.untyped_storage().data_ptr() not in non_cudagraph_inps
559             ]
560         )
561 
562         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts and not self.already_warm:
563             out_refs = self.path_live_weakrefs()
564             new_storages = [
565                 t for t in out_refs if t.data_ptr() not in non_cudagraph_inps
566             ]
567             check_memory_pool(self.device_index, self.cuda_graphs_pool, new_storages)
568 
569         return out
570 
571     def path_live_weakrefs(self) -> Generator[StorageWeakRefWrapper]:
572         "Returns all live storages weakrefs that created by nodes in this path"
573         for stor_ref, _ in self.path_live_weakrefs_and_stacktraces():
574             yield stor_ref
575 
576     def path_live_weakrefs_and_stacktraces(
577         self,
578     ) -> Generator[Tuple[StorageWeakRefWrapper, Optional[str]]]:
579         nodes = []
580         node = self
581         while node:
582             nodes.append(node)
583             node = node.parent
584 
585         for node in reversed(nodes):
586             for i, output in enumerate(node.outputs_weakrefs):
587                 if is_live(output):
588                     yield output, (node.stack_traces[i] if node.stack_traces else None)
589 
590     def all_outputs_are_dead(self):
591         return not list(self.path_live_weakrefs())

632 class CUDAGraphNode:
633     """
634     A single recording of a function into a CUDA Graph. Recordings of CUDA Graphs share a single memory pool
635     and are structured into a tree, where there is a single recording that can precede it (parent) and multiple
636     subsequent recordings that may follow (children). A node will have no parent if it is the first recording
637     in a tree; i.e., when it is first recorded, there are no live tensors from a previous recording which
638     would force a dependency.
639 
640     On first recording, all of the live tensors in the current CUDA Graph Node path will be
641     reflected in the corresponding private pool. On subsequent executions, the caching allocator
642     is unaffected when the graph is replayed.
643 
644     In order to support recording a subsequent cuda graph recording after execution of this graph,
645     we checkpoint the state of the memory pool so that it may later be resumed.
646 
647     WrappedFunction should have already been warmed up prior to invocation.
648 
649     See [setCheckpointPoolState] for further explanation, as well as
650     https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13564/222815509-374f3400-f83d-4f7d-8fa6-4a092b3250bb.png
651     """
652 
653     def __init__(
654         self,
655         wrapped_function: WrappedFunction,
656         id: GraphID,
657         parent: Optional[CUDAGraphNode],
658         inputs: List[Tensor],
659         cuda_graphs_pool: Tuple[int, int],
660         device_index: int,
661         stack_traces: Optional[StackTraces],
662         stream: torch.cuda.Stream,
663     ):
664         assert isinstance(inputs, (list, tuple))
665 
666         self.wrapped_function = wrapped_function
667         self.id = id
668         self.device = device_index
669         self.stack_traces = stack_traces
670         self.stream = stream
671 
672         # if this is a root parent will be None. use weakref to prevent reference cycle
673         self._parent = weakref.ref(parent) if parent is not None else None
674         # reference to the shared memory pool for the entire cuda graphs tree
675         self.cuda_graphs_pool = cuda_graphs_pool
676 
677         # A single wrapped function may be recorded multiple times if memory patterns or
678         # invariants change from one execution to the next
679         self.children: Dict[FunctionID, List[CUDAGraphNode]] = defaultdict(list)
680 
681         # StorageWeakRef maintains whether the Storage C++ object remains allocated,
682         # not whether the corresponding memory has been deallocated. In order
683         # to use them to track memory deallocations we must maintain a single StorageWeakRef
684         # for all Storages that reference that memory (even if we are constructing Storages
685         # that do not have a deallocator function). We maintain one single storage_cache
686         # as we execute any tree path. When we retrieve a storage from the cache we
687         # check that it is still alive, and we hash based on observed recording data ptr
688         # and storage cdata.
689 
690         # we preserve a single reference to executed outputs that is then referenced
691         # in children to avoid children having to chase parent pointers in the hot path
692         # DO NOT reassign output_weakrefs, only call `clear()`
693         # Path is a series of nodes from root to the current node
694         self.outputs_weakrefs: OutputList[Optional[StorageWeakRefWrapper]] = []
695         self.path_weakrefs: LevelList[OutputList[Optional[StorageWeakRefWrapper]]] = [
696             node.outputs_weakrefs for node in self._path_from_root
697         ]
698         self.path_stacktraces: LevelList[StackTraces] = [
699             node.stack_traces for node in self._path_from_root
700         ]
701 
702         # tensors which are outputs of previous graphs in the tree
703         self.cudagraph_managed_idxs: List[int] = [
704             idx
705             for idx, t in enumerate(inputs)
706             if self._is_cuda_graph_recorded_tensor(t)
707         ]
708 
709         self.static_input_idxs: List[int] = list(
710             set(wrapped_function.static_input_idxs) | set(self.cudagraph_managed_idxs)
711         )
712 
713         self.static_input_data_ptrs: InputList[int] = [
714             (inputs[i].data_ptr() if i in self.static_input_idxs else None)
715             for i in range(len(inputs))
716         ]
717 
718         # When we checkpoint, and free generations, we will be manually freeing the outputs
719         # of CUDAGraphNodes. We should not be freeing parameters, not do we need to account for
720         # their liveness (they are static), so we need to compute which outputs are aliases of
721         # parameters. Some static inputs are saved tensors from the forward that die in the backward.
722         # Their locations are static but lifetimes are not. We only include the persistent static
723         # data ptrs below because the non persistent data ptrs may be outputs of this record and
724         # fresh allocations.
725 
726         # precompute expanded dims to avoid computing in the hot path
727         self.expanded_dims: List[List[int]] = [
728             get_expanded_dims(x) if idx not in self.static_input_idxs else []
729             for idx, x in enumerate(inputs)
730         ]
731 
732         # For each node in path, which outputs were observed to be live
733         # before invoking graph recording, and after graph recording
734         self.recorded_liveness_before_graph: LevelList[OutputList[bool]] = []
735         self.recorded_liveness_after_graph: LevelList[OutputList[bool]] = []
736 
737         # List of Tuples of (depth, output_index) that index into node at depth
738         # number of nodes from root and output_index of outputs. Will index into
739         # path_weakrefs.
740         self.expected_dead_indices_before_graph: List[PathOutputIndex] = []
741         self.expected_dead_indices_after_graph: List[PathOutputIndex] = []
742 
743         # all live indices after graph recording
744         self.live_indices_after_graph: List[PathOutputIndex] = []
745 
746         if self.parent is not None:
747             previous_liveness = self.parent.recorded_liveness_after_graph
748             curr_liveness = self._get_liveness(self.path_weakrefs)
749 
750             different_indices = self._get_different_indices(
751                 previous_liveness, curr_liveness
752             )
753 
754             self.recorded_liveness_before_graph = curr_liveness
755             self.expected_dead_indices_before_graph = different_indices
756 
757         recording_inputs = self._allocate_and_copy_recording_inputs(inputs)
758         # recording inputs will copy over memory, so we can free non recording inputs
759         inputs.clear()
760         del inputs
761 
762         # graph used for recording model invocation
763         self.graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
764 
765         # we allocate non-static inputs within the same memory pool as the CUDAGraph
766         # which we will record the model with. For memory efficiency, it is important
767         # to reclaim the input memory when the inputs are no longer live. To accomplish this,
768         # we reconstruct tensors at the correct data pointers of our inputs which are
769         # non owning and do not prevent deallocation. On subsequent executions, input values
770         # will be copied over to these tensors.
771         self.reconstructed_inputs: InputList[Tensor] = [
772             self._reconstruct_from_tensor_metadata(self._tensor_metadata(x))
773             for x in recording_inputs
774         ]
775 
776         # DO THE RECORDING!!!
777         # We record the CUDA graph in the constructor of CUDAGraphNode, which
778         # gives you what the CPU side compute of the function would do.  We
779         # don't throw the recording outputs away: their memory is
780         # correctly accounted for in the CUDAGraphs caching allocator.  This
781         # means on the very FIRST run of the CUDA graph node, we can directly
782         # do more recording, because we have a valid caching allocator state.
783         # NB: This relies on run() being called immediately after the
784         # constructor, otherwise this optimization would not be valid.
785 
786         # initialized below in _record
787 
788         self.checkpointed_caching_state: Optional[AllocatorState] = None
789 
790         # Output Storage Alias information, can be:
791         # - A new, unaliased storage, or the output is None
792         # - An alias of an output of a prior graph
793         # - An alias of an output already created in the reconstructed outputs
794         self.output_storage_alias: OutputList[OutputAliasInfo] = []
795 
796         # is the output Storage unaliased in subsequent outputs, of all subsequent paths
797         # if it is, we cached the output tensor and adjust storage liveness tracking to also
798         # check if the output tensor does not have an additional python reference.
799         # If a descendent node discovers it has an alias of a prior output, then the output
800         # will no longer be cached in the ancestor.
801         # The large majority of tensors are unaliased, and preserving aliased output tensors would add
802         # significant additional complexity with marginal gains
803         # The cached tensor outputs are added on the first execution, and cleared whenever we need
804         # to do subsequent recording
805         self.unaliased_in_all_paths: OutputList[bool] = []
806         self.cached_tensor_outputs: OutputList[Optional[Tensor]] = []
807 
808         # if an output aliases a static, persistent input then the corresponding Tensor will
809         # be set here. These are different than cached tensors, because they are tensors that
810         # are aliases of parameters that are always live.
811         self.static_output_tensors: OutputList[Optional[Tensor]] = []
812 
813         self.recording_outputs: OutputList[Optional[torch.Tensor]] = self._record(
814             wrapped_function.model, recording_inputs
815         )
816         self.outputs_metadata: OutputList[Optional[Dict[str, Any]]] = []
817 
818         # As with inputs, we do not want to keep the outputs permanently alive because that would prevent
819         # their memory being reclaimed in subsequent cuda graph recordings. We record the tensor metadata
820         # needed to reconstruct instead.
821         for out in self.recording_outputs:
822             if isinstance(out, torch.Tensor):
823                 self.outputs_metadata.append(
824                     self._tensor_metadata(out, ignore_storage_offset=False)
825                 )
826             else:
827                 assert out is None
828                 self.outputs_metadata.append(None)
829 
830         self.graph.replay()
831 
832     def _copy_input(self, idx, dst, src):
833         expanded_dims = self.expanded_dims[idx]
834         dst = index_expanded_dims(dst, expanded_dims)
835         src = index_expanded_dims(src, expanded_dims)
836         # TODO - one jit kernel across multiple inputs
837         dst.copy_(src)
838 
839     def run_first_inputs(self, new_inputs):
840         if config.triton.fast_path_cudagraph_asserts:
841             self.debug_check_invariants_before_invocation()
842 
843         # graph is already invoked in the __init__
844         # inputs are copied over in _allocate_recording_inputs and subsequently cleared
845         assert len(new_inputs) == 0
846         outputs = self.recording_outputs
847         self.recording_outputs = None
848         return outputs
849 
850     def run(self, new_inputs):
851         if config.triton.fast_path_cudagraph_asserts:
852             self.debug_check_invariants_before_invocation()
853 
854         assert len(self.static_input_data_ptrs) == len(new_inputs)
855         # NB: this ranges over non-static inputs too
856         for idx, data_ptr in enumerate(self.static_input_data_ptrs):
857             if idx in self.cudagraph_managed_idxs:
858                 continue
859             if data_ptr is not None:
860                 # static input, e.g., parameter
861                 assert data_ptr == new_inputs[idx].data_ptr()
862             else:
863                 # non-static input, need to copy it into CUDA graph
864                 dst = self.reconstructed_inputs[idx]
865                 src = new_inputs[idx]
866                 self._copy_input(idx, dst, src)
867 
868         new_inputs.clear()
869         self.run_graph()
870 
871         outputs = self.reconstruct_outputs()
872         self.debug_check_invariants_after_invocation()
873 
874         return outputs
875 
876     def reconstruct_outputs(self):
877         "Reconstruct output tensors according to their saved metadata and alias information"
878 
879         # Cached tensors will not yet be set on the first execution
880         # They are also cleared in checkpointing, so if we checkpoint this node
881         # and then execute it again we will need to repopulate cached tensors
882         if not self.cached_tensor_outputs:
883             self._initialize_cached_tensors()
884 
885         outputs = []
886 
887         for i, (storage_info, metadata) in enumerate(
888             zip(self.output_storage_alias, self.outputs_metadata)
889         ):
890             if metadata is None:
891                 outputs.append(None)
892                 continue
893 
894             cached_t = self.cached_tensor_outputs[i]
895             if cached_t is not None:
896                 # No need to update weakrefs, already correctly initialized
897                 outputs.append(cached_t)
898                 continue
899 
900             static_t = self.static_output_tensors[i]
901             if static_t is not None:
902                 assert self.outputs_weakrefs[i] is None

907                 storage_info, metadata

911                 out = self._reconstruct_from_tensor_metadata(metadata, storage)

913                 assert isinstance(storage, int)

915                     metadata, outputs[storage].untyped_storage()

962     def _record(self, model, inputs):
963         "Record the model"
964 
965         # see: output_is_alias_of_persistent_static_inputs above
966         static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs: Dict[int, StorageWeakRefWrapper] = {
967             inputs[i].untyped_storage().data_ptr(): StorageWeakRefWrapper(inputs[i])
968             for i in self.wrapped_function.static_input_idxs
969             if not self._is_cuda_graph_recorded_tensor(inputs[i])
970         }
971 
972         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts:
973             # need to use parent live weakrefs because live_indices isnt set yet
974             memory = (
975                 [] if self.parent is None else list(self.parent.path_live_weakrefs())
976             )
977             memory += [
978                 StorageWeakRefWrapper(elem)
979                 for i, elem in enumerate(inputs)
980                 if i not in self.wrapped_function.static_input_idxs
981             ]
982             check_memory_pool(self.device, self.cuda_graphs_pool, memory)
983 
984         with preserve_rng_state(), torch.cuda.device(
985             self.device
986         ), clear_cublas_manager(), torch.cuda.graph(
987             self.graph, stream=self.stream, pool=self.cuda_graphs_pool
988         ), get_history_recording():
989             static_outputs = model(inputs)
990 
991         # running model should reclaim memory
992         assert len(inputs) == 0
993 
994         if not isinstance(static_outputs, (list, tuple)):
995             static_outputs = (static_outputs,)
996 
997         self._add_first_outputs(static_outputs, static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs)
998 
999         return static_outputs

1001     def _add_first_outputs(
1002         self,
1003         outputs,
1004         static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs: Dict[int, StorageWeakRefWrapper],
1005     ):
1006         "Add the outputs from the first invocation of the node and set up metadata"
1007 
1008         # getting liveness before we have added the outputs to path, so the length
1009         # of the two lists is equal
1010         prev_liveness = self.recorded_liveness_before_graph
1011         curr_liveness = self._get_liveness(self.path_weakrefs)
1012 
1013         delta = self._get_different_indices(prev_liveness, curr_liveness)
1014         self.expected_dead_indices_after_graph = delta
1015 
1016         assert len(self.outputs_weakrefs) == 0
1017         # index from data pointer to index in outputs
1018         output_new_storages_index: Dict[StorageDataPtr, int] = {}
1019 
1020         self.unaliased_in_all_paths = [False for _ in range(len(outputs))]
1021         self.static_output_tensors = [None for _ in range(len(outputs))]
1022 
1023         for i, o in enumerate(outputs):
1024             if o is None:
1025                 self.output_storage_alias.append(UnaliasedStorage)
1026                 continue
1027 
1028             ref = static_input_persistent_storage_ptrs.get(
1029                 o.untyped_storage().data_ptr(), None
1030             )
1031             if ref and ref() is not None:
1032                 self.output_storage_alias.append(None)
1033                 self.static_output_tensors[i] = o
1034                 continue
1035 
1036             path_ref = self._is_alias_of_live_recorded_tensor(o)
1037             if path_ref is not None:
1038                 self._mark_prior_graph_output_as_aliased(path_ref)
1039                 self.output_storage_alias.append(AliasesPriorGraphOutput(path_ref))
1040                 continue
1041 
1042             if o.untyped_storage().data_ptr() in output_new_storages_index:
1043                 index = output_new_storages_index[o.untyped_storage().data_ptr()]
1044                 self.unaliased_in_all_paths[index] = False
1045                 self.output_storage_alias.append(AliasesNewOutput(index))
1046                 continue
1047 
1048             output_new_storages_index[o.untyped_storage().data_ptr()] = i
1049             self.output_storage_alias.append(UnaliasedStorage)
1050             self.unaliased_in_all_paths[i] = True
1051 
1052         if self.stack_traces is None:
1053             self.stack_traces = [None for _ in range(len(outputs))]
1054         else:
1055             assert len(self.stack_traces) == len(
1056                 outputs
1057             ), "Wrong number of stack traces passed in"
1058 
1059         assert not self.outputs_weakrefs
1060         for out, static_output_tensor in zip(outputs, self.static_output_tensors):
1061             if out is None or static_output_tensor is not None:
1062                 self.outputs_weakrefs.append(None)
1063             else:
1064                 self.outputs_weakrefs.append(StorageWeakRefWrapper(out))
1065 
1066         self.recorded_liveness_after_graph = self._get_liveness(self.path_weakrefs)
1067         self.checkpointed_caching_state = torch._C._cuda_getCheckpointState(
1068             self.device, self.cuda_graphs_pool
1069         )
1070 
1071         # now, get liveness with outputs added
1072         for depth in range(len(self.path_weakrefs)):
1073             for output_index in range(len(self.path_weakrefs[depth])):
1074                 if is_live(self.path_weakrefs[depth][output_index]):
1075                     self.live_indices_after_graph.append((depth, output_index))
1076 
1077         self.debug_check_invariants_after_invocation()
1078         if config.triton.slow_path_cudagraph_asserts:
1079             check_memory_pool(
1080                 self.device, self.cuda_graphs_pool, list(self.path_live_weakrefs())
1081             )

1090     def _initialize_cached_tensors(self):
1091         # we should not be clearing output_weakrefs, and they should be set in the first
1092         # record run
1093         assert len(self.outputs_weakrefs) == len(self.outputs_metadata)
1094 
1095         for i, (storage_info, metadata, make_cached) in enumerate(
1096             zip(
1097                 self.output_storage_alias,
1098                 self.outputs_metadata,
1099                 self.unaliased_in_all_paths,
1100             )
1101         ):
1102             if not make_cached:
1103                 self.cached_tensor_outputs.append(None)
1104                 continue
1105 
1106             assert storage_info is UnaliasedStorage
1107             s = self.create_storage(metadata)
1108             out = self._reconstruct_from_tensor_metadata(metadata, storage=s)
1109 
1110             # XXX: let autograd know that there will be an additional reference to the tensor
1111             # that can be ignored when deciding whether to do gradient buffer inplacing.
1112             # Otherwise, inplacing could differ between tracing and subsequent execution.
1113             # For some models we tested this led to inputs no longer being in cudagraph pools,
1114             # leading to spurious re-recordings.
1115             # It also tells AMP cache that even though the tensor impls cannot be cached
1116             # in dtype conversions.
1117 
1118             torch._C._add_cached_tensor(out)
1119 
1120             self_ref = weakref.ref(self)
1121 
1122             # one reference in our array, and calling sys.getrefcount bumps the refcount by one
1123             def check_refcount(i):
1124                 return self_ref().get_output_refcount(i) == 2
1125 
1126             check = functools.partial(check_refcount, i=i)
1127 
1128             self.outputs_weakrefs[i] = StorageWeakRefWrapper(out, extra_ref_check=check)
1129             self.cached_tensor_outputs.append(out)

1153     def _is_cuda_graph_recorded_tensor(self, t: torch.Tensor):

1191     @staticmethod

1193         prev: List[List[bool]], curr: List[List[bool]]
1194     ) -> List[PathOutputIndex]:

1196         dead_indices = []

1199             assert len(outputs1) == len(outputs2)
1200             for j, (output1, output2) in enumerate(zip(outputs1, outputs2)):
1201                 if output1 != output2:

1348     def _allocate_and_copy_recording_inputs(self, inputs):
1349         """
1350         Allocate inputs for non static, non cudagraph managraphed managed tensors in the memory pool
1351         and copy over the tensor values.
1352         """
1353 
1354         torch.cuda.synchronize()
1355         self.stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
1356         recording_inputs = []
1357 
1358         with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True), torch.cuda.device(
1359             self.device
1360         ), _use_cuda_memory_pool_manager(
1361             self.device,
1362             mem_pool=self.cuda_graphs_pool,
1363             stream=self.stream,
1364         ):
1365             for i, inp in enumerate(inputs):
1366                 if i not in self.static_input_idxs:
1367                     # static_input does an allocation!
1368                     recording_inputs.append(static_input(inp))
1369                     # copy over and clear non recording input
1370                     self._copy_input(i, recording_inputs[-1], inp)
1371                     inputs[i] = None
1372                     del inp
1373                 else:
1374                     recording_inputs.append(inp)
1375 
1376         return recording_inputs

1378     def check_invariants(self, inputs: List[Tensor]) -> bool:
1379         """
1380         Checks if this node can be run. The same pattern of tensor liveness and tensors
1381         managed in the cudagraph private pool must remain stable.
1382         """
1383 
1384         # previously managed data pointers remain stable
1385         for idx in self.cudagraph_managed_idxs:
1386             if inputs[idx].data_ptr() != self.static_input_data_ptrs[idx]:
1387                 return False
1388 
1389         if not self._check_liveness(
1390             self.expected_dead_indices_before_graph, self.path_weakrefs
1391         ):
1392             return False
1393 
1394         # the cudagraph managed tensors which died upon recording must also die upon
1395         # this invocation. it is too late to check after we've replayed the graph,
1396         # because we would have already written over their memory.
1397         for idx in self.cudagraph_managed_idxs:
1398             inputs[idx] = None
1399 
1400         check(
1401             self._check_liveness(
1402                 self.expected_dead_indices_after_graph, self.path_weakrefs
1403             ),
1404             lambda: "TODO: graph recording observed an input tensor deallocate during graph "
1405             " recording that did not occur during replay. Please file an issue.",
1406         )
1407         return True

1419 def get_cudagraph_segments(pool_id):

1424 def get_block_addrs(pool_id, live_only=True):
1425     blocks = []
1426 
1427     for segment in get_cudagraph_segments(pool_id):
1428         addr = segment["address"]
1429         for block in segment["blocks"]:
1430             if block["state"] == "active_allocated" or not live_only:
1431                 blocks.append(addr)
1432 
1433             addr += block["size"]
1434 
1435     return blocks

1438 def format_tb(caching_allocator_trace):
1439     formatted_traceback = []
1440 
1441     MAX_LENGTH = 20
1442 
1443     for entry in caching_allocator_trace["frames"][0:MAX_LENGTH]:
1444         formatted_traceback.append(
1445             traceback.FrameSummary(entry["filename"], entry["line"], entry["name"])
1446         )

1451 def check_memory_pool(device, pool_id, live_storages_ptrs: List[StorageWeakRefWrapper]):
1452     assert all(
1453         isinstance(elem, StorageWeakRefWrapper) for elem in live_storages_ptrs
1454     )  # noqa: C419
1455     unique_storages = {stor.data_ptr() for stor in live_storages_ptrs if stor()}
1456 
1457     # check if there is a divergence first, then do the expensive snapshot call after
1458     # we know it will error
1459     if torch._C._cuda_checkPoolLiveAllocations(device, pool_id, unique_storages):
1460         return
1461 
1462     segments = get_cudagraph_segments(pool_id)
1463 
1464     allocated_not_in_live_storages = {}
1465 
1466     for segment in segments:
1467         addr = segment["address"]
1468         for block in segment["blocks"]:
1469             if block["state"] == "active_allocated":
1470                 if addr not in unique_storages:
1471                     allocated_not_in_live_storages[addr] = block
1472                 else:
1473                     unique_storages.remove(addr)
1474 
1475             addr += block["size"]
1476 
1477     check(
1478         len(unique_storages) == 0,
1479         lambda: f"These storage data ptrs are not allocated in pool {pool_id} but should be {unique_storages}",
1480     )
1481 
1482     if allocated_not_in_live_storages != 0:
1483         formatted = []
1484         for dp, block in allocated_not_in_live_storages.items():
1485             trace = (
1486                 format_tb(block["history"][-1]) if block.get("history", None) else None
1487             )
1488             formatted.append(f"Data Pointer: {dp}, history: \n{trace}")
1489         formatted_s = "\n".join(formatted)
1490         msg = (
1491             f"These live storage data ptrs are in the cudagraph pool but not "
1492             f"accounted for as an output of cudagraph trees: \n\n{formatted_s}"
1493         )
1494         raise RuntimeError(msg)

1521     to follow the same order and have the same output tensor livespans. To remove

1523     the tree manager will end a currently recording tree whenever it is valid - when
1524     the memory pool no longer has any live allocations.

1532     If we were to warm up the model and keep an extra copy of the inputs around to subsequently
1533     use for recording, we would incur a memory penalty. Additionally, if we are part way through training
1534     your model and need to recompile, memory will be allocated to the cuda graph pool, so we run this

# Idiom 567 (Context-Aware Variables)

Definition: introduces context variables that allow managing context-local state in a way that works well with asynchronous code, replacing or supplementing thread-local storage.

Rationale: thread-local state does not propagate correctly across asynchronous tasks, leading to unexpected behavior and bugs. Violations occur when code continues to use thread-local variables instead of leveraging context variables,

# With PEP567: Using ContextVar for proper context-local state in asynchronous environments
from contextvars import ContextVar

context_var = ContextVar('value')

def set_context(value):

def get_context():
    return context_var.get()

def check_js_threshold_version(working_alias):
    # type: (str) -> bool
    """
    Check if the nodeJS engine version on the system with the allowed minimum version.

    https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#nodejs-changelog
    """
    # parse nodejs version into int Tuple: 'v4.2.6\n' -> [4, 2, 6]
    current_version_str = subprocess.check_output(
        [working_alias, "-v"]).decode('utf-8')

    current_version = [int(v) for v in current_version_str.strip().strip('v').split('.')]
    minimum_node_version = [int(v) for v in minimum_node_version_str.split('.')]

    return current_version >= minimum_node_version


def new_js_proc(js_text, force_docker_pull=False):
    # type: (Text, bool) -> subprocess.Popen

    required_node_version, docker = (False,)*2
    nodejs = None

    for n in trynodes:
        try:
            if subprocess.check_output([n, "--eval", "process.stdout.write('t')"]).decode('utf-8') != "t":
                continue
            else:
                nodejs = subprocess.Popen([n, "--eval", js_text],
                                          stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                          stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
                processes_to_kill.append(nodejs)
                required_node_version = check_js_threshold_version(n)
                break
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError):
            pass

    if nodejs is None or nodejs is not None and required_node_version is False:
        try:
            nodeimg = "node:slim"

            if not have_node_slim:
                dockerimgs = subprocess.check_output(["docker", "images", "-q", nodeimg]).decode('utf-8')
                # if output is an empty string
                if (len(dockerimgs.split("\n")) <= 1) or force_docker_pull:
                    # pull node:slim docker container
                    nodejsimg = subprocess.check_output(["docker", "pull", nodeimg]).decode('utf-8')
                    _logger.info("Pulled Docker image %s %s", nodeimg, nodejsimg)
                have_node_slim = True

                                       "--attach=STDIN", "--attach=STDOUT", "--attach=STDERR",
                                       "--sig-proxy=true", "--interactive",
                                       "--rm", nodeimg, "node", "--eval", js_text],
                                      stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
            processes_to_kill.append(nodejs)
            docker = True
        except OSError as e:
            if e.errno == errno.ENOENT:
                pass
            else:

        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            pass

    # docker failed and nodejs not on system
    if nodejs is None:

            u"docker run node:slim".format(u", ".join(trynodes)))

    if docker is False and required_node_version is False:

"""Evaluate CWL Javascript Expressions in a sandbox."""
from __future__ import absolute_import

import errno
import json
import os
import re
import select
import sys
import threading
from io import BytesIO
from typing import cast, Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

import six
from future.utils import raise_from
from pkg_resources import resource_stream
from typing_extensions import Text  # pylint: disable=unused-import
# move to a regular typing import when Python 3.3-3.6 is no longer supported

from schema_salad.utils import json_dumps

from .loghandler import _logger
from .utils import onWindows, processes_to_kill, subprocess
try:
    import queue  # type: ignore
except ImportError:
    import Queue as queue  # type: ignore


class JavascriptException(Exception):
    pass


JSON = Union[Dict[Text, Any], List[Any], Text, int, float, bool, None]

localdata = threading.local()

default_timeout = 20
have_node_slim = False
# minimum acceptable version of nodejs engine
minimum_node_version_str = '0.10.26'

def check_js_threshold_version(working_alias):
    # type: (str) -> bool
    """
    Check if the nodeJS engine version on the system with the allowed minimum version.

    https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#nodejs-changelog
    """
    # parse nodejs version into int Tuple: 'v4.2.6\n' -> [4, 2, 6]
    current_version_str = subprocess.check_output(
        [working_alias, "-v"]).decode('utf-8')

    current_version = [int(v) for v in current_version_str.strip().strip('v').split('.')]
    minimum_node_version = [int(v) for v in minimum_node_version_str.split('.')]

    return current_version >= minimum_node_version


def new_js_proc(js_text, force_docker_pull=False):
    # type: (Text, bool) -> subprocess.Popen

    required_node_version, docker = (False,)*2
    nodejs = None
    trynodes = ("nodejs", "node")
    for n in trynodes:
        try:
            if subprocess.check_output([n, "--eval", "process.stdout.write('t')"]).decode('utf-8') != "t":
                continue
            else:
                nodejs = subprocess.Popen([n, "--eval", js_text],
                                          stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
                                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                          stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
                processes_to_kill.append(nodejs)
                required_node_version = check_js_threshold_version(n)
                break
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError):
            pass

    if nodejs is None or nodejs is not None and required_node_version is False:
        try:
            nodeimg = "node:slim"
            global have_node_slim

            if not have_node_slim:
                dockerimgs = subprocess.check_output(["docker", "images", "-q", nodeimg]).decode('utf-8')
                # if output is an empty string
                if (len(dockerimgs.split("\n")) <= 1) or force_docker_pull:
                    # pull node:slim docker container
                    nodejsimg = subprocess.check_output(["docker", "pull", nodeimg]).decode('utf-8')
                    _logger.info("Pulled Docker image %s %s", nodeimg, nodejsimg)
                have_node_slim = True
            nodejs = subprocess.Popen(["docker", "run",
                                       "--attach=STDIN", "--attach=STDOUT", "--attach=STDERR",
                                       "--sig-proxy=true", "--interactive",
                                       "--rm", nodeimg, "node", "--eval", js_text],
                                      stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
            processes_to_kill.append(nodejs)
            docker = True
        except OSError as e:
            if e.errno == errno.ENOENT:
                pass
            else:
                raise
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            pass

    # docker failed and nodejs not on system
    if nodejs is None:
        raise JavascriptException(
            u"cwltool requires Node.js engine to evaluate and validate "
            u"Javascript expressions, but couldn't find it.  Tried {}, "
            u"docker run node:slim".format(u", ".join(trynodes)))

    # docker failed, but nodejs is installed on system but the version is below the required version
    if docker is False and required_node_version is False:
        raise JavascriptException(
            u'cwltool requires minimum v{} version of Node.js engine.'.format(
                minimum_node_version_str),
            u'Try updating: https://docs.npmjs.com/getting-started/installing-node')

    return nodejs

PROCESS_FINISHED_STR = "r1cepzbhUTxtykz5XTC4\n"

def exec_js_process(js_text,                  # type: Text
                    timeout=default_timeout,  # type: float
                    js_console=False,         # type: bool
                    context=None,             # type: Optional[Text]
                    force_docker_pull=False,  # type: bool
                   ):
    # type: (...) -> Tuple[int, Text, Text]

    if not hasattr(localdata, "procs"):
        localdata.procs = {}

    if js_console and context is not None:
        raise NotImplementedError("js_console=True and context not implemented")

    if js_console:
        js_engine = 'cwlNodeEngineJSConsole.js'
        _logger.warning(
            "Running with support for javascript console in expressions (DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION)")
    elif context is not None:
        js_engine = "cwlNodeEngineWithContext.js"
    else:
        js_engine = 'cwlNodeEngine.js'

    created_new_process = False

    if context is not None:
        nodejs = localdata.procs.get((js_engine, context))
    else:
        nodejs = localdata.procs.get(js_engine)

    if nodejs is None \
            or nodejs.poll() is not None \
            or onWindows():
        res = resource_stream(__name__, js_engine)
        js_engine_code = res.read().decode('utf-8')

        created_new_process = True

        new_proc = new_js_proc(js_engine_code, force_docker_pull=force_docker_pull)

        if context is None:
            localdata.procs[js_engine] = new_proc
            nodejs = new_proc
        else:
            localdata.procs[(js_engine, context)] = new_proc
            nodejs = new_proc

    killed = []

    def terminate():  # type: () -> None
        """Kill the node process if it exceeds timeout limit."""
        try:
            killed.append(True)
            nodejs.kill()
        except OSError:
            pass

    timer = threading.Timer(timeout, terminate)
    timer.daemon = True
    timer.start()

    stdin_text = u""
    if created_new_process and context is not None:
        stdin_text = json_dumps(context) + "\n"
    stdin_text += json_dumps(js_text) + "\n"

    stdin_buf = BytesIO(stdin_text.encode('utf-8'))
    stdout_buf = BytesIO()
    stderr_buf = BytesIO()

    rselect = [nodejs.stdout, nodejs.stderr]  # type: List[BytesIO]
    wselect = [nodejs.stdin]  # type: List[BytesIO]


    def process_finished():  # type: () -> bool
        return stdout_buf.getvalue().decode('utf-8').endswith(PROCESS_FINISHED_STR) and \
            stderr_buf.getvalue().decode('utf-8').endswith(PROCESS_FINISHED_STR)

    # On windows system standard input/output are not handled properly by select module
    # (modules like  pywin32, msvcrt, gevent don't work either)
    if sys.platform == 'win32':
        READ_BYTES_SIZE = 512

        # creating queue for reading from a thread to queue
        input_queue = queue.Queue()
        output_queue = queue.Queue()
        error_queue = queue.Queue()

        # To tell threads that output has ended and threads can safely exit
        no_more_output = threading.Lock()
        no_more_output.acquire()
        no_more_error = threading.Lock()
        no_more_error.acquire()

        # put constructed command to input queue which then will be passed to nodejs's stdin
        def put_input(input_queue):
            while True:
                buf = stdin_buf.read(READ_BYTES_SIZE)
                if buf:
                    input_queue.put(buf)
                else:
                    break

        # get the output from nodejs's stdout and continue till output ends
        def get_output(output_queue):
            while not no_more_output.acquire(False):
                buf = os.read(nodejs.stdout.fileno(), READ_BYTES_SIZE)
                if buf:
                    output_queue.put(buf)

        # get the output from nodejs's stderr and continue till error output ends
        def get_error(error_queue):
            while not no_more_error.acquire(False):
                buf = os.read(nodejs.stderr.fileno(), READ_BYTES_SIZE)
                if buf:
                    error_queue.put(buf)

        # Threads managing nodejs.stdin, nodejs.stdout and nodejs.stderr respectively
        input_thread = threading.Thread(target=put_input, args=(input_queue,))
        input_thread.daemon = True
        input_thread.start()
        output_thread = threading.Thread(target=get_output, args=(output_queue,))
        output_thread.daemon = True
        output_thread.start()
        error_thread = threading.Thread(target=get_error, args=(error_queue,))
        error_thread.daemon = True
        error_thread.start()

        finished = False

        while not finished and timer.is_alive():
            try:
                if nodejs.stdin in wselect:
                    if not input_queue.empty():
                        os.write(nodejs.stdin.fileno(), input_queue.get())
                    elif not input_thread.is_alive():
                        wselect = []
                if nodejs.stdout in rselect:
                    if not output_queue.empty():
                        stdout_buf.write(output_queue.get())

                if nodejs.stderr in rselect:
                    if not error_queue.empty():
                        stderr_buf.write(error_queue.get())

                if process_finished() and error_queue.empty() and output_queue.empty():
                    finished = True
                    no_more_output.release()
                    no_more_error.release()
            except OSError:
                break

    else:
        while not process_finished() and timer.is_alive():
            rready, wready, _ = select.select(rselect, wselect, [])
            try:
                if nodejs.stdin in wready:
                    buf = stdin_buf.read(select.PIPE_BUF)
                    if buf:
                        os.write(nodejs.stdin.fileno(), buf)
                for pipes in ((nodejs.stdout, stdout_buf), (nodejs.stderr, stderr_buf)):
                    if pipes[0] in rready:
                        buf = os.read(pipes[0].fileno(), select.PIPE_BUF)
                        if buf:
                            pipes[1].write(buf)
            except OSError:
                break
    timer.cancel()

    stdin_buf.close()
    stdoutdata = stdout_buf.getvalue()[:-len(PROCESS_FINISHED_STR) - 1]
    stderrdata = stderr_buf.getvalue()[:-len(PROCESS_FINISHED_STR) - 1]

    nodejs.poll()

    if nodejs.poll() not in (None, 0):
        if killed:
            returncode = -1
        else:
            returncode = nodejs.returncode
    else:
        returncode = 0
        # On windows currently a new instance of nodejs process is used due to
        # problem with blocking on read operation on windows
        if onWindows():
            nodejs.kill()

    return returncode, stdoutdata.decode('utf-8'), stderrdata.decode('utf-8')

def code_fragment_to_js(jscript, jslib=""):
    # type: (Text, Text) -> Text
    if isinstance(jscript, six.string_types) \
            and len(jscript) > 1 and jscript[0] == '{':
        inner_js = jscript
    else:
        inner_js = "{return (%s);}" % jscript

    return u"\"use strict\";\n{}\n(function(){})()".format(jslib, inner_js)

def execjs(js,                       # type: Text
           jslib,                    # type: Text
           timeout,                  # type: float
           force_docker_pull=False,  # type: bool
           debug=False,              # type: bool
           js_console=False          # type: bool
          ):  # type: (...) -> JSON

    fn = code_fragment_to_js(js, jslib)

    returncode, stdout, stderr = exec_js_process(
        fn, timeout, js_console=js_console,
        force_docker_pull=force_docker_pull)

    if js_console:
        if stderr is not None:
            _logger.info("Javascript console output:")
            _logger.info("----------------------------------------")
            _logger.info('\n'.join(re.findall(
                r'^[[](?:log|err)[]].*$', stderr, flags=re.MULTILINE)))
            _logger.info("----------------------------------------")

    def stdfmt(data):  # type: (Text) -> Text
        if "\n" in data:
            return "\n" + data.strip()
        return data

    def fn_linenum():  # type: () -> Text
        lines = fn.splitlines()
        ofs = 0
        maxlines = 99
        if len(lines) > maxlines:
            ofs = len(lines) - maxlines
            lines = lines[-maxlines:]
        return u"\n".join(u"%02i %s" % (i + ofs + 1, b) for i, b in enumerate(lines))

    if returncode != 0:
        if debug:
            info = u"returncode was: %s\nscript was:\n%s\nstdout was: %s\nstderr was: %s\n" %\
                (returncode, fn_linenum(), stdfmt(stdout), stdfmt(stderr))
        else:
            info = u"Javascript expression was: %s\nstdout was: %s\nstderr was: %s" %\
                (js, stdfmt(stdout), stdfmt(stderr))

        if returncode == -1:
            raise JavascriptException(
                u"Long-running script killed after {} seconds: {}".format(
                    timeout, info))
        else:
            raise JavascriptException(info)

    try:
        return cast(JSON, json.loads(stdout))
    except ValueError as err:
        raise_from(JavascriptException(
            u"{}\nscript was:\n{}\nstdout was: '{}'\nstderr was: '{}'\n".format(
                err, fn_linenum(), stdout, stderr)), err)

# Idiom 584 (Dictionary Union Operator)

Definition: Introduces | and |= operators for a more concise and intuitive syntax that mirrors set operations, providing a consistent and clear way to merge dictionaries.

Rationale: Using dictionary unpacking ({**dict1, **dict2}), is verbose and creates a new dictionary each time, whereas using dict.update() modifies a dictionary in-place and returns None. Both methods pos challenges for readability and functional programming practices. 

Example:

d2 = {'c': 3, 'd': 4}
merged = d1.copy()  
merged.update(d2)
d1 = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}

d1 = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}

  def __init__(self, url):
    # Convert the url back into a profile canonical name.
    profile = url.split(server_stubs.REKALL_PROFILE_REPOSITORY_VERSION + "/")[1]
    profile = profile.split(".")[0]

  def read(self):
    FakeHandle.read_count += 1

    server = rekall_test_lib.TestRekallRepositoryProfileServer()
    profile = server.GetProfileByName(
        profile_name, version=server_stubs.REKALL_PROFILE_REPOSITORY_VERSION)

def FakeOpen(url, timeout=None):  # pylint: disable=invalid-name
  _ = timeout

class ProfileServerTest(test_lib.GRRBaseTest):

    super(ProfileServerTest, self).setUp()

  def testProfileFetching(self):

    profile_name = "nt/GUID/F8E2A8B5C9B74BF4A6E4A48F180099942"

    FakeHandle.read_count = 0

    with utils.Stubber(urllib2, "urlopen", FakeOpen):

    # This time it should have been cached.
    self.assertEqual(FakeHandle.read_count, 1)

  def testGzExtension(self):
    with utils.Stubber(urllib2, "urlopen", FakeOpen):
      profile = self.server.GetProfileByName("pe")
      # We received compressed data.
      zlib.decompress(profile.data, 16 + zlib.MAX_WBITS)

      # We issued one http request.
      self.assertEqual(FakeHandle.read_count, 1)

      self.server.GetProfileByName("pe")

      # This time it should have been cached.
      self.assertEqual(FakeHandle.read_count, 1)

      self.server.GetProfileByName("pe")

      # This is the same profile.
      self.assertEqual(FakeHandle.read_count, 1)

    cache_urn = rdfvalue.RDFURN(config.CONFIG["Rekall.profile_cache_urn"])
    cached_items = list(
        aff4.FACTORY.Open(
            cache_urn.Add(server_stubs.REKALL_PROFILE_REPOSITORY_VERSION),
            token=self.token).ListChildren())

    # We cache the .gz only.
    self.assertEqual(len(cached_items), 1)
    self.assertEqual(cached_items[0].Basename(), "pe")


def main(args):
  test_lib.main(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
  flags.StartMain(main)

"""
CUDA graph trees are a safety abstraction over CUDAGraphs, similar to make_graph_callables,
which share the same memory pool.  Sharing a memory pool is an extremely
important optimization when chaining multiple CUDA graphs together, as it
prevents you from needing to copy intermediate tensors from one graph to the
next, and reduces overall memory usage by allowing dead memory from the first
pool to be reused in the second.

The standard graph/make_graph_callables support sharing memory pool, but
with a lot of caveats.  CUDA graph trees remove these restrictions:

* Previously, if you recorded graphs A, B, you had to replay A, B in that
  order.  With CUDA graph trees, after replaying A, you can change your
  mind and record/replay a different graph B'; we will support efficient
  execution of both A, B and A, B', using only max(mem(A, B), mem(A, B')).  In
  other words: we support arbitrary trees of CUDA graph operations, not just
  sequences (this is why this feature is called CUDA graph trees.)

* Previously, if you executed graph A, some non-CUDA graph code, and then
  graph B, after executing graph B, it was not safe to retain any references
  to intermediates produced by A.  With CUDA graph trees, we track if any
  outputs of graph A are still live by the time graph B is run, and make
  sure graph B doesn't clobber there memory when reusing the CUDA graphs
  pool.  You'll get a separate recording of B depending on what tensors
  stay live or dead.

CUDA graph trees are flexible enough to be used in Dynamo across graph breaks,
which is their primary use case.

The ability to switch from replay to record is fairly nontrivial: remember that
when you replay a CUDA graph, you only replay CUDA operations; no CPU side state
is updated.  In particular, the CPU-side book-keeping for the allocator is not
reconstructed.  However, to record a new child CUDA graph, we must restore this
book-keeping.  This is what checkpoint pool state is used for.
"""

    """
    Cublas keeps a persistent workspace allocation for running matmuls. This poses a problem for
    doing warmup within a CUDAGraph private pool because we do not want persistent allocations from
    one one run to the next. When we begin a new run of a cudagraphs path (generation), all tensors
    from the previous generation are freed. This frees them the the memory pool, but not elsewhere.
    A tensor in the cublas workspace would continue to be in use the workspace but would also get allocated
    in the next run. The memory would be in use in two places.

    To solve this, we clear cublas caches before and after warming up or recording. If a workspace is required
